painpoint.name: Accurate 3D ground truth needs instrumentation that alters the scene

evidence.latest_state: The strongest recent result is SHOW3D (Rim et al., Meta, CVPR 2026). It uses a back-mounted rig of 8 exocentric cameras plus a Quest 3 headset, and nothing is attached to the hands or objects. Against a 30-camera dome reference, its hand annotations reach 6.28-7.90 mm median MPJPE; for hand-object interaction the figures are 7.90 mm median and 12.53 mm P90. Against manual in-the-wild labels the median is 5.65-6.36 mm, with a hand-object P90 of 16.48 mm. Against mocap-tracked objects, object translation P50 is 1.53-3.51 mm and rotation P50 is 1.23-5.77 deg. However, only 1.9M of 4.3M frames survive confidence filtering, object yield is 53.5-93 percent, and the authors report three failures: missed hands under hand-object or hand-hand occlusion, lost objects outdoors, and unresolved azimuth for symmetric objects. In effect, the accuracy holds only on the frames the pipeline keeps, so the realism-versus-accuracy trade-off is shifted rather than removed. GigaHands (CVPR 2025) scales markerless capture with a 51-camera dome (34 h, 183M frames, 417 objects) but reports no quantitative validation against mocap. Marker and sensor routes remain the accuracy reference and continue to grow: HOT3D (CVPR 2025) uses optical markers, and MR6D and MTevent (2025) use Vicon. The glove route (Glove2Hand, CVPR 2026 Highlight) synthesizes bare hands from gloved video, and AVI-HT (arXiv 2026) fuses vision with glove IMUs. Some work drops dense 3D ground truth altogether: EPIC-Contact (ECCV 2026) annotates contact points, and AnyHand (arXiv 2026) is synthetic. A CVPR 2026 workshop dataset with Vicon ground truth reports that state-of-the-art markerless capture degrades substantially under severe occlusion. No 2025-2026 paper found gives a camera-invisible measurement channel with millimetre accuracy for natural, moving, single-camera bimanual manipulation; UV invisible markers exist only for deformable surfaces (DOT).

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: SHOW3D: Capturing Scenes of 3D Hands and Objects in the Wild
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Captures in the wild without markers, using a mobile back-mounted 8-camera rig plus a VR headset and ego-exo fusion with confidence filtering. Hands reach 6-8 mm median MPJPE against a 30-camera dome; objects reach 1.5-3.5 mm translation P50 against mocap. 1.9M of 4.3M frames are usable, and occluded hands and symmetric objects fail.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Ego-Exo 3D Hand Tracking in the Wild with a Mobile Multi-Camera Rig
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Hand-only predecessor of SHOW3D: the same mobile rig of 8 exocentric cameras plus a Quest 3, aimed at reducing the trade-off between realism and annotation accuracy.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: GigaHands: A Massive Annotated Dataset of Bimanual Hand Activities
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Fully automatic markerless bimanual hand and object annotation from a 51-camera RGB dome (YOLOv8, HaMeR, triangulation, MANO fitting), totalling 34 h and 183M frames. It is not validated quantitatively against mocap.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: HOT3D: Hand and Object Tracking in 3D from Egocentric Multi-View Videos
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Egocentric hand and object ground truth from professional optical mocap with small markers on hands and objects. 1.16M of 1.5M frames pass visual inspection. It represents the marker-based accuracy reference.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Glove2Hand: Synthesizing Natural Hand-Object Interaction from Multi-Modal Sensing Gloves
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Converts video of sensing-glove hand-object interaction into photorealistic bare-hand video with a 3D Gaussian hand model and diffusion restoration, which removes the appearance change caused by gloves. The HandSense dataset pairs the video with tactile and IMU signals, and the IMU poses give ground truth under occlusion.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: AVI-HT: Adaptive Vision-IMU Fusion for 3D Hand Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Adaptively fuses an egocentric camera with 6-DoF IMUs worn on a glove, and introduces DexGloveHOI (100K+ vision-IMU samples). It reports a 16.1 percent lower keypoint error than prior methods.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Towards in-the-wild Egocentric 3D Hand-Object Pose Estimation (EPIC-Contact, HOPformer)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Bypasses instrumentation by converting annotated contact points into posed 3D hand-object meshes for 62.3K in-the-wild EPIC frames, a weaker form of supervision. It reports 82.4 percent success on ARCTIC.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: A Dataset and Evaluation for Complex 4D Markerless Human Motion Capture
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Multi-view RGB-D dataset with Vicon ground truth plus SMPL/SMPL-X fits for multi-person scenes with severe occlusion. It shows that state-of-the-art markerless methods degrade substantially under these conditions.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: AnyHand: A Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for RGB(-D) Hand Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Synthetic route: 2.5M single-hand and 4.1M hand-object RGB-D images with exact labels. Adding them to training improves results on FreiHAND and HO-3D.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: XYZ-IBD: High-precision Bin-picking Dataset for Object 6D Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Reaches millimetre-level static 6D labels using anti-reflection spray, multi-view depth fusion and semi-automatic annotation. This shows that accurate labels still need scene alteration and static objects.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: MR6D: Benchmarking 6D Pose Estimation for Mobile Robots
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Obtains 6D ground truth for static and dynamic subsets with Vicon mocap, using eye-in-hand and object calibration, which ties dynamic-object labels to a mocap room.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: VinT-6D: A Large-Scale Object-in-hand Dataset from Vision, Touch and Proprioception
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Object-in-hand pose data for robot hands from simulation (2M frames) and a custom real platform (0.1M frames) with touch and proprioception. It sidesteps ground truth for human hands.

evidence.crowdedness: HIGH. Every major hand and object dataset group publishes on this capture-versus-accuracy trade-off each year: Meta Reality Labs with HOT3D, the ego-exo rig and SHOW3D; Brown with GigaHands; Bristol, MPI and Damen-Black with EPIC-Contact; plus sensor-glove groups and the 6D-pose and BOP groups. Most of the work is large engineering projects (domes, mobile rigs, mocap).
evidence.trend: rising. Attention is moving from lab domes to in-the-wild capture (SHOW3D, CVPR 2026) and to substitutes for instrumentation: glove-to-bare-hand synthesis, vision-IMU fusion, contact-based weak labels and large synthetic sets. Demand for accurate in-the-wild 3D hand-object data is driven by robot learning, egocentric AI and world models.

skeptics.reasons:
I found no 2025-2026 work that solves P01. Recent work does remove several of its sub-claims, so the statement is too broad as written.

1) The "confined to labs" and "dense domes" parts have weakened. SHOW3D (arXiv 2603.28760, Meta and Yale, March 2026) uses an 8 kg backpack with 8 exocentric cameras plus a Quest 3 headset. It labels hands and objects in the wild with off-the-shelf foundation models: Sapiens and InterNet keypoints, then CNOS, FoundPose and GoTrack for objects. It reports median hand error of 5.65-6.28 mm and object P50 translation error of 1.53-3.51 mm against mocap. But the headset pose still comes from 5 mocap cameras. It needs CAD models of the objects and covers only 21 HOT3D objects, and its object validation used 5 objects. Its stated failure modes are severe occlusion, hand-object interpenetration and symmetry ambiguity under occlusion. Those are exactly the P01 conditions.

2) Hand-only scale is close to engineering. EgoDex (arXiv 2505.11709, Apple, 2025) has 829 h of 3D hand and upper-body pose tracked on the Apple Vision Pro. It has no object pose ground truth, and its hand labels are on-device tracker outputs, not independently validated.

3) Monocular reconstruction pipelines are not ground truth. AGILE (arXiv 2602.04672, SIGGRAPH 2026) and Open4DHOI / 4DHOISolver (arXiv 2512.00960) give plausible reconstructions from in-the-wild video. They are validated only on the instrumented benchmarks (HO3D, DexYCB, ARCTIC, BEHAVE, IMHD2). AGILE generates the object mesh, and 4DHOISolver fails on sliding contact and deformable objects. The pseudo-label route therefore still depends on instrumented datasets for its accuracy claims.

4) Measurement channels the camera cannot see already exist: UV-fluorescent invisible markers (DOT, TPAMI 2025; LUV, IROS 2022) and active IR markers (EgoPressure). So the "why it persists" claim that no such channel exists is false as stated. But these need controlled UV or IR lighting and a fixed rig, so they do not scale outside the lab either.

Net: the instrumentation burden has fallen sharply for rigid, pre-scanned objects. What is left is millimetre ground truth for unscanned, articulated or deformable objects under contact and heavy occlusion, captured with a single everyday camera. A second open part is how to certify how accurate the pseudo-labels from these foundation-model annotators are, when they are checked only on a few objects against mocap.

skeptics.reframe: For rigid, pre-scanned objects, foundation-model pseudo-labels from a portable multi-camera rig (SHOW3D) now get within a few millimetres of mocap. So the problem is no longer simply "instrumentation alters the scene". Two things remain unsolved. First, there is no way to get, or to certify, millimetre-accurate 3D labels for hands and unscanned, articulated or deformable objects during contact and heavy occlusion from one everyday or RGB-D camera. Second, the pseudo-labels that annotators of this kind produce come with no per-frame error bound, and their accuracy is checked only against small mocap subsets.

skeptics.reasons:
The artifact charge does not hold. I mapped the 107 supporting records to titles. They come from many independent groups and settings: MPI/Tuebingen (ARCTIC, BEHAVE, InterCap, EMDB), Meta Reality Labs (HOT3D, Nymeria, Ego-Exo4D, emg2pose), SJTU (OakInk2), Tsinghua (TACO, HOI4D), TUM (PhoCaL, HouseCat6D), NVIDIA (HANDAL), ShanghaiTech (NeuralDome, HOI-M3) and surgical groups (POV-Surgery, MICCAI 2023). The venues include CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICRA, IROS, T-RO, TPAMI, IJCV and MICCAI. The sensing setups also differ: optical markers, IMU suits, electromagnetic sensors, dense RGB domes, multi-Kinect rigs, robot-arm and IR-tracker 6D labelling, and mobile backpack rigs. Three subcommunities (hand-object, body-object, object pose) state the trade-off independently, so it is not tied to one dataset or one lab's convention.

Three narrower points cut the claim down without refuting it.

(1) Genre bias. The corpus is mostly dataset and benchmark papers, and that genre is expected to justify its capture design. A realism-versus-accuracy discussion is therefore close to obligatory there, which inflates the paper count relative to how much the trade-off blocks method papers.

(2) The word "only" in the statement is too strong. Other communities have partly solved the "alters the scene" half. Computational photography uses UV-fluorescent markers that cameras cannot see under normal light; DOT (ICCP 2024, TPAMI special issue) tracks hands and deformable objects with them, and LUV (2022) uses the same idea for robot manipulation labels. EMDB uses small electromagnetic sensors as a non-optical channel. The object-pose community has largely moved training off real annotation: the BOP 2023 report states that the gap between methods trained only on synthetic PBR images and methods also trained on real images "noticeably shrank". These counterexamples contradict the statement's "why it persists" sentence, which says no invisible measurement channel exists. What remains unsolved is scale and mobility: invisible-marker and EM rigs are still lab-bound, need special lighting or hardware, and have not been shown for natural, in-contact, occluded bimanual manipulation at scale.

(3) For training data, the problem is increasingly avoided with synthetic data and pseudo-labels. The real residual bottleneck is evaluation ground truth for occluded, in-contact, moving hands and objects outside the lab. Example: DynOPETs validates its annotation against mocap on only 10 sequences.

So the pain point is field-wide but stated too broadly. Its strongest and least artifact-prone form is a measurement and evaluation bottleneck, not a training-data claim.

skeptics.reframe: Scene-altering instrumentation is no longer the core obstacle: invisible UV markers, electromagnetic sensors and synthetic PBR data each work around it in the lab. The obstacle that survives is that no method yet gives millimetre-accurate, independently validated 3D ground truth for the occluded, in-contact, moving state of hands and objects outside instrumented rooms. As a result, single-camera and RGB-D hand-object trackers are evaluated on lab-bound data or on pseudo-labels that are themselves unvalidated, so their real-world accuracy under contact and occlusion cannot be measured.

skeptics.reasons:
Skeptic 3, "no research question", argued for refutation but did not succeed. The case for refutation is real. Much of P01 as written is a description of resources and engineering. Accuracy improves predictably with more instrumentation: ARCTIC hand error falls from 49.0 to 23.4 mm as views go from 2 to 8, HMDO from 14.75 to 5.58 mm as views go from 4 to 10, and AssemblyHands from 27.55 to 4.20 mm with multi-view. The listed fixes (backpack rigs, anti-reflection spray, artist cleanup, SAM2 plus manual correction, robot-arm or stop-and-go capture) are mostly known procedures that trade cost against realism. Taken literally, a request for a larger, more natural, mm-accurate dataset is a wish for money and capture hours, and a reviewer would treat another such dataset as incremental.

Three research questions survive, and each has top-venue precedent.
(1) Annotation as an inference problem. HOnnotate (CVPR 2020) was accepted for an annotation method: joint optimisation of hand and object poses across all frames with few RGB-D views. That makes "what is the minimum sensing from which occluded, in-contact hand-object state is identifiable to a stated accuracy, and how do we certify each label" a method question, not a budget item.
(2) Evaluation under imperfect ground truth. Brachmann et al. (ICCV 2021) showed that method rankings in re-localisation flip depending on which pseudo-GT reference algorithm is used. P01's own evidence shows the same exposure in hand-object and 6D work: DynOPETs labels are validated against mocap on only 10 extra sequences, BundleTrack propagation needs manual fixes every ten frames, and SfM or ARKit alignment leaves centimetre errors. Whether current hand-object and moving-object benchmarks can tell methods apart at their reported mm-level differences is unanswered and publishable.
(3) A measurement channel the evaluated camera cannot see. The why_it_persists field already names this. Time-multiplexed UV-fluorescent invisible markers give ground-truth correspondences on unmarked frames for deformable objects and hands (Li et al., ICCP 2024, the DOT dataset). That venue is not on the target list, so extending the idea to rigid and articulated hand-object 6D pose under contact, with a quantified label error budget, is an open contribution.

The reframed question is not about obtaining more labels. It asks whether label accuracy can be decoupled from scene alteration, through invisible channels or self-certifying optimisation, and how much current benchmark conclusions depend on unquantified label error. A CVPR or ICCV reviewer would accept that as a significant question. The score stays moderate because a dataset-only contribution would still be judged engineering, and a single-camera or single RGB-D thesis setup limits what can be validated without a high-accuracy reference rig.

skeptics.reframe: Can 3D hand and object labels for natural manipulation be made accurate without changing what the camera sees? Two routes are open. One is a sensing channel the evaluated camera cannot see, such as time-multiplexed UV-fluorescent or IR markers. The other is a self-certifying optimisation that outputs a per-frame error bound for occluded, in-contact states. In both cases the label error must be quantified well enough to show whether current hand-object and moving-object benchmarks can separate methods at the mm-level differences they report.

research_questions.question: RQ1. Reference dependence of hand-object benchmarks. When the 3D reference used to score hand and hand-object pose methods is itself an annotator's output (markerless multi-view fits or foundation-model pseudo-labels), how much do method rankings and reported millimetre gains change with the choice of reference? And do methods trained on one annotator's labels inherit that annotator's systematic errors and get rewarded for them?
research_questions.why_top_venue: New hand-object datasets now rank methods whose differences are sub-millimetre to a few millimetres. Yet their references carry errors of the same order or larger. SHOW3D's hand labels are 6.28-7.90 mm median against a 30-camera dome, with a 12.53 mm P90 for hand-object frames. GigaHands has no mocap validation. DexYCB reports a 2D reprojection error of about 4-5 px against human labels. DynOPETs is validated against mocap on only 10 sequences. Brachmann et al. (ICCV 2021) showed that relocalisation rankings flip with the pseudo-GT algorithm, a result that changed how that field reports. Two targeted searches this session found no hand-object analogue, but absence is not verified. A measured flip rate, a minimum detectable difference that exceeds typical claimed gains, or evidence of label-bias absorption would change reporting practice across the field. This is the bottleneck skeptic 2 kept: evaluation ground truth, not training data. It is also research question (2) of skeptic 3, and it needs no capture hardware.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) Take public datasets that hold two kinds of reference: a marker or mocap reference plus raw multi-view images (ARCTIC, HOT3D), or a markerless fit plus independent human 2D labels (DexYCB). (2) Rebuild markerless references R_k from k views with a SHOW3D-style off-the-shelf recipe: 2D hand keypoints (HaMeR/WiLoR/Sapiens class), triangulation, a MANO fit, and CAD-based object pose (FoundationPose class) fused across views. Measure each R_k against mocap, stratified by occlusion fraction, contact proximity and hand-hand overlap. (3) Score a panel of public single-view checkpoints against mocap and against every R_k. Report Kendall tau, the pairwise flip rate, and the minimum detectable difference (MDD) per metric from a paired bootstrap with a fitted label-error model. (4) Label-bias absorption test as a 2x2 design: fine-tune one light model on mocap labels and, separately, on R_k labels, then score both models against both references. (5) Deliverables: a reference-uncertainty map per benchmark frame, a reporting protocol (MDD plus occlusion-stratified error), and a noise-aware metric that discounts error below the local reference uncertainty.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: On the ARCTIC validation split, use the mocap-fitted MANO and object poses as R_mocap. Build R_2, R_4 and R_8 from the allocentric views. Evaluate at least 6 public hand or hand-object models on the egocentric view against all four references. Report the rank correlation, the flip rate, the MDD and the per-bin reference error. Add the 2x2 fine-tuning test with one small backbone. Go/no-go at about month 4: if the reference error is below the spread between methods in every occlusion bin, turn the paper into the MDD and reporting-protocol contribution, then extend to HOT3D (egocentric mocap) and DexYCB (markerless, with human 2D labels).
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data only: ARCTIC (mocap plus 8 allocentric views and 1 egocentric view), HOT3D (mocap, Aria/Quest streams) and DexYCB (8 RealSense views, markerless labels, human 2D keypoints). SHOW3D only if its dome-validated subset is released (not verified). One 24-48 GB GPU: most of the work is inference, plus one small fine-tune. Terabyte-scale storage for full-resolution multi-view images; subsets suffice. No camera, mocap or robot needed.
research_questions.risks: (a) Null result: rankings may be stable. Mitigation: the MDD and stratified-error protocol remains publishable, but at a weaker level (NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks rather than a CVPR main track). (b) The mocap reference has its own error (skin and marker offsets, MANO fitting), so it is a better reference, not truth, and must carry its own error bars. (c) Hidden test splits (HO3D, ARCTIC leaderboard, HOT3D challenge sets) force use of validation splits and re-running methods. (d) Reproducing many checkpoints costs a lot of engineering. (e) Reviewers may call it analysis-only, so it needs actionable tools. (f) The groups that own the instrumented data (Meta, MPI) could publish their own audit first.

research_questions.question: RQ2. Certified pseudo-labels. Can a hand-object annotator (a few RGB views or a single RGB-D view) output a calibrated per-frame error bound (for example 90 percent coverage on joint error and on object translation and rotation error) whose coverage holds within each occlusion and contact bin and under a change of dataset? Pseudo-labels could then be kept or weighted by certified accuracy instead of heuristic confidence.
research_questions.why_top_venue: SHOW3D keeps 1.9M of 4.3M frames through confidence filtering and checks accuracy only on small mocap or dome subsets. Its yield is 53.5-93 percent for objects, and its failures fall exactly under occlusion and symmetry. Skeptic 1's residual open problem is that pseudo-labels carry no per-frame error bound. The closest work is SLUE (Shaikewitz, Georgiou, Carlone; T-RO; arXiv 2511.21666, verified this session), which gives distribution-free ellipsoidal bounds for rigid object pose from keypoint noise bounds. CUPS (arXiv 2412.10431, title seen in search) conformalizes human pose and shape. No coupled bound for articulated hand plus object under contact was found (absence not verified). HOnnotate (CVPR 2020) is precedent that an annotation method, not just a dataset, is accepted at a top venue.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) Nonconformity scores on 2D keypoints and object correspondences, calibrated against mocap-referenced frames. Use Mondrian/conditional conformal bins over visibility, contact proximity, view count and depth validity. (2) Propagate the bounds to 3D. For the object, use SLUE-style convex ellipsoidal bounds. For the hand, use set-membership over MANO poses consistent with the keypoint bounds and with non-penetration and contact constraints, or, as a cheaper baseline, conformalized quantile regression on 3D error from annotator features (multi-view disagreement, depth residual, temporal inconsistency). (3) Handle dataset shift with weighted conformal, using domain-classifier density-ratio weights. Report leave-one-dataset-out coverage. (4) Use: yield-versus-certified-accuracy curves, compared with SHOW3D-style heuristic filtering, ensembles and MC dropout. Also compare training a tracker on certified subsets versus confidence-filtered subsets of equal size.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Objects first: calibrate on ARCTIC mocap and test on HOT3D mocap. Report empirical coverage against nominal per occlusion bin and the median bound size, against three baselines (heuristic confidence, deep ensemble, unconditional split conformal). Then hands with the same protocol. Success means coverage within a few points of nominal in every bin, plus bounds tight enough to separate the method differences measured in RQ1. Set that threshold from RQ1's numbers rather than now.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: ARCTIC and HOT3D (mocap references) for calibration and testing. DexYCB or HO3D for the single RGB-D variant, where the reference is itself markerless, which requires a noisy-reference conformal correction or treatment as secondary evidence. Few public RGB-D hand-object sets have mocap; this is a real gap, which RQ3 addresses. One 24-48 GB GPU. Convex solvers on CPU.
research_questions.risks: (a) Under heavy occlusion the bounds may be too wide to be useful, which is the frames that matter most. (b) Exchangeability breaks across datasets, and weighted conformal can be unstable when calibration sets are small. (c) The reference error of mocap is comparable to tight bounds. (d) Overlap with SLUE: novelty must come from articulated-hand plus contact coupling and from occlusion-conditional coverage, and the Carlone group could extend SLUE to hands first. (e) Reviewers may read it as applying conformal prediction unless the use case (certified training subsets, benchmark filtering) shows a measurable gain.

research_questions.question: RQ3. A camera-invisible channel in a commodity sensor. Can the near-infrared stereo imagers already inside a consumer RGB-D camera (with emitter on/off interleaving) read fiducials embedded in hand-held objects, such as NIR-transmitting-filament air-gap codes or NIR-fluorescent inserts, that the RGB stream cannot see? And would the resulting 6D object ground truth be accurate enough to evaluate single-camera hand-object trackers, and to supply calibration data for RQ2 that is exchangeable with deployment, in the tracker's own domain?
research_questions.why_top_venue: P01's why_it_persists names the missing camera-invisible measurement channel. The invisible channels that exist need special lighting or rigs. DOT (ICCP 2024 / TPAMI, verified) uses time-multiplexed UV-fluorescent dyes with multi-camera capture, on rope, paper, cloth and hands, not rigid hand-held objects. LUV (2022) uses UV for robot labels. HCI tags (InfraredTags, arXiv 2202.06165; BrightMarker, MIT; iMarkers, arXiv 2501.15505, verified) have not been used as vision ground truth for hand-object pose (not found in this session's searches; unverified). The conceptual hook is that conformal calibration needs ground truth on data exchangeable with deployment. Visible markers break this, since paper 88 in P01 reports that trackers can learn markers. An invisible channel restores it. As a standalone paper this is more likely robotics-venue work; it reaches CVPR or ICCV only when combined with RQ2. Note that skeptic 1's claim that EgoPressure uses active IR markers is not supported by its abstract (multi-view Kinect optimisation), checked this session.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) 3D-print replicas of a few benchmark-style objects with NIR fiducials on several faces. (2) Run the RGB-D camera with emitter interleaving: emitter-off frames give clean NIR images for multi-tag PnP, and emitter-on frames give depth. Fuse PnP with depth-to-CAD ICP for metric pose, and map the result into the RGB frame through factory extrinsics refined with a visible calibration board. (3) Error budget: static poses on a jig against a visible ArUco board. Dynamic cross-check with a second camera that sees a visible marker on the object face hidden from the evaluated camera, and a borrowed robot arm if available. (4) RGB-invisibility test: paired comparison of detector and FoundationPose behaviour on tagged versus untagged twin objects. (5) Record a modest bimanual handling set, evaluate single-view trackers by occlusion fraction, and export the frames as RQ2 calibration data.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: One object and one RGB-D camera. (a) Static translation and rotation error versus distance and visible-tag fraction, against the jig and ArUco reference. (b) A paired RGB-invisibility test. (c) 20-30 minutes of handling, with FoundationPose-class error versus occlusion scored against the NIR reference. Go/no-go: the NIR reference error must be clearly below tracker error in the occluded bins, otherwise it is not a reference.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: A RealSense D435-class camera with accessible NIR streams. Emitter interleaving support and whether the RGB imager blocks NIR must be checked on the actual unit (not verified here). An FDM printer, low-cost NIR-transmitting or NIR-fluorescent filament, an optional NIR long-pass filter, and a second RGB-D camera for the cross-check. A borrowed robot arm is optional. One GPU.
research_questions.risks: (a) It covers objects only, not hands, which leaves the hard half of P01 open. (b) Printed replicas differ in material from real objects, which weakens the realism claim. (c) Single-view NIR PnP depth error may not be well below RGB-D tracker error. (d) The grasping hand occludes the tags, so many tag faces are needed. (e) The projector pattern and the visible-band sensitivity of the NIR imagers may reduce tag contrast. (f) HCI prior art means novelty must lie in the measurement-science and calibration use. (g) The dataset would be small and single-lab.

fit.thesis_assets_help: Small edge, mostly for RQ3, some framing for RQ2, none for RQ1. (1) The single RealSense D435 desk setup and the causal 30 fps capture-and-pose chain can host the NIR channel of RQ3 without building a new rig. The D435's NIR stereo imagers are the proposed invisible channel, but emitter interleaving and the RGB NIR-blocking behaviour must be checked on the unit. (2) The ArUco metric-pose pipeline and its calibration give RQ3 its static validation reference. The thesis's own visibly marked object is a ready example of scene-altering instrumentation, usable as the visible-marker arm of the RGB-invisibility test. (3) The measured/held/constrained honesty labels are a qualitative precursor of RQ2's per-frame certified bounds. They help the framing and offer a small demonstration, but they are not calibrated and carry no coverage evidence. (4) The object-conditioned recovery of the occluded holding arm, the Unity twin and the 28 recordings of one subject give no top-venue edge for P01. The recordings come from one subject, the marker is visible in RGB, and there is no independent reference at millimetre accuracy, so they can serve as pilot data at most.
fit.what_a_small_lab_cannot_do_here: It cannot compete on the capture side of P01, which is crowded and resource-bound: dense domes (GigaHands' 51 cameras, SHOW3D's 30-camera reference dome), mocap rooms (HOT3D, ARCTIC, MR6D), mobile 8-camera ego-exo rigs (SHOW3D), sensing-glove platforms, or multi-subject datasets at scale. It cannot produce independently validated millimetre ground truth for hands (as opposed to rigid objects) under contact and occlusion without borrowing mocap. Nor can it claim millimetre accuracy for its own captures without a borrowed reference such as mocap or a robot arm. It cannot extend to many object categories or to deformable and articulated objects within 12-18 months. It cannot access hidden test labels (HO3D, ARCTIC leaderboard, HOT3D challenge splits), and it cannot train foundation-scale annotators. The viable route is to work on evaluation and certification using other groups' instrumented public data (RQ1, RQ2), plus at most one cheap invisible-channel instrument for rigid objects (RQ3). A new dataset paper as the main contribution would be judged incremental against Meta, Brown and MPI.

painpoint.name: Objects without a template or category prior

evidence.latest_state: Between 2025 and 2026, priors from foundation models and image-to-3D or novel-view-synthesis diffusion models largely replaced pre-scanned templates. The core gap is still open: with a model-free, everyday object that is being handled, accuracy remains far below model-based. In BOP 2024 the model-free 6D detection track on BOP-H3 (HOT3D, HOPEv2, HANDAL) received no submissions, and no entry used dynamic hand-manipulation onboarding. The only model-free 2D detection entry, GFreeDet, reached 31.9 AP against 30.3 for model-based CNOS. Per-dataset AP was HOT3D 33.8, HOPEv2 36.4 and HANDAL 25.5 (arXiv 2504.02812). Model-free tracks ran again in BOP 2025 (awards announced at ICCV 2025, November 2025), but I could not verify their results or submission counts. IndustryShapes (ICRA 2026) still reports FoundationPose at 0.25 AR model-free against 0.67 with CAD. Any6D (CVPR 2025) works from a single RGB-D anchor: on HO3D it gets 38.3 AR and 98.7 ADD-S but only 40.4 ADD (Oryon gets 1.0 AR), and its accuracy degrades when the generated shape is wrong because shapes are not updated. On hand-object reconstruction: MagicHOI (ICCV 2025) uses diffusion priors for unseen object regions, HOSt3R (arXiv 2025) reports state of the art on SHOWMe without keypoints or intrinsics, ForeHOI (arXiv 2026) is feed-forward and about 100x faster, and Grasp in Gaussians (arXiv 2026) is 4.4x to 38.9x faster using a SAM3D initialisation. For two hands, BIGS (CVPR 2025) is still the main template-free monocular method for ARCTIC. CARI4D (CVPR 2026) reports +38% in-distribution and +36% on unseen data for category-agnostic body-object 4D reconstruction. For category-level pose, Object Pose Transformer (arXiv 2026) reports state of the art on Omni6DPose, HouseCat6D and NOCS, but I found no 2025-2026 source showing the Omni6D collapse on unseen categories (best 3.24% 5deg2cm) has been fixed. EgoAERO (arXiv 2026) reaches CAD-comparable reconstruction on HOI4D for robot learning, using RGB-D and masks only. PANY (ECCV 2026) gains +12% on YCB-V and over +20% on LM-O with sparse references.

evidence.crowdedness: HIGH: I found at least 15 papers from 2025-2026 at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, CoRL and ICRA or on arXiv. They come from well-resourced groups: NVIDIA (FoundationPose and Any6D authors, and CARI4D), ETH/AIT (MagicHOI), Naver Labs/INRIA (HOSt3R), TUM/Busam (PANY, OPT), MPI/Theobalt (Grasp in Gaussians), MIT (Point2Pose) and the BOP organisers. The single-object, single-hand, rigid sub-problem is crowded. The bimanual, dynamically onboarded, hand-occluded corner is much less crowded.
evidence.trend: Rising. Image-to-3D, SAM3D and novel-view diffusion priors, together with pointmap foundation models (DUSt3R/VGGT-style), made template-free pipelines practical in 2025-2026. BOP added and kept model-free tracks with HOT3D hand-manipulation onboarding, and robot learning from human video needs object motion without assets. A 2026 survey on hand-object interaction with foundation models (arXiv 2607.28394) frames generalisation to unseen objects as a central open challenge.

skeptics.reasons: P02 is not refuted, but 2025-2026 work has removed much of it. Three parts of the original claim are weaker now. (1) Single-view onboarding is now a real option. Any6D (CVPR 2025) estimates 6D pose and size from one RGB-D anchor image and is evaluated on HO3D and YCBInEOAT. OnePoseViaGen (CoRL 2025 oral) generates a 3D model from one image, aligns its scale and pose, and was demonstrated with real-robot dexterous grasping. SAM 3D Objects (Meta, Nov 2025) returns a textured mesh plus object pose from one occluded image in seconds. As a result, "generate a mesh, then track it with FoundationPose" is now routine engineering. The 0.25 vs 0.67 AR gap cited from IndustryShapes probably overstates the current gap, though I did not find a newer head-to-head number. (2) Template-free hand-object reconstruction now covers bimanual scenes and is faster. BIGS (CVPR 2025) reconstructs two hands with an unknown object from monocular video using diffusion SDS priors. GHOST (arXiv 2603.18912) reports being an order of magnitude faster than earlier category-agnostic methods. Grasp in Gaussians (arXiv 2604.12929) initialises from SAM 3D and runs 4.4x to 38.9x faster than prior work. That weakens the evidence items saying HOLD handles only one hand and fails on bimanual scenes. (3) Category-level and model-free paradigms are starting to merge. Object Pose Transformer (arXiv 2603.23370, preprint) claims state of the art on Omni6DPose and HouseCat6D with a single model, but I could not verify its numbers, so the vocabulary-collapse figures (62.52 to 14.42 percent; 3.24 percent on unseen categories) may be out of date. Why it is still not solved: (a) "Is Single-View Mesh Reconstruction Ready for Robotics?" (arXiv 2505.17966; the abstract page says BMVC 2026) concludes that current single-view reconstruction fails robotics requirements on occlusion robustness, collision-ready geometry, typical robot inputs and real-time compute. (b) BIGS relies on per-sequence SDS optimisation and is offline. GHOST and Grasp in Gaussians are single-hand and assume a rigid object; Grasp in Gaussians depends on SAM 3D initialisation quality. (c) Generate-then-track pipelines freeze a mesh made from one early, often hand-occluded view and never update it, so regrasps and newly revealed surfaces are not corrected. (d) I could not verify any BOP 2025 result for model-free 6D detection with dynamic (hand-manipulation) onboarding on BOP-H3. The challenge page confirms the track ran and awards were posted on 2025-11-16, but the leaderboard pages I reached did not show model-free entries, so I found no evidence that this gap is closed. (e) None of the work found does online, metric-scale, joint shape-and-pose tracking of an unscanned object under bimanual occlusion with RGB-D at interactive rates. Net: the category-level vocabulary sub-claim and the claim that no usable template-free pipeline exists are largely outdated. The core problem in bimanual, occluded, online settings survives.

skeptics.reframe: Objects without a template can now be onboarded from one view by generating a mesh (SAM 3D Objects, OnePoseViaGen, Any6D) and then tracking it. Offline template-free reconstruction now covers bimanual scenes (BIGS). The open problem is online, metric-scale RGB-D tracking that refines the object's shape and 6D pose together while the object is handled by two hands. The generated or partial template is made from a hand-occluded view and has to be corrected as surfaces become visible. The tracking has to survive regrasps, handovers and textureless or small objects. It must run at interactive rates so a digital twin or robot demonstration can use it. Current pipelines freeze an initial generated mesh, optimise offline per sequence, or assume one hand and a rigid grasp. The category-level vocabulary scaling sub-claim should be dropped or rechecked, because unified unseen-object models (for example Object Pose Transformer) now target it.

skeptics.reasons:
The artifact critique does not refute the core of P02, but it removes several of the supporting claims.

Diversity check: why the core is not an artifact. The 69 supporting papers come from many separate groups and communities that do not share one dataset:
- MPI/Tuebingen body-object capture (BEHAVE, InterCap, RHOBIN, PICO)
- NAVER Labs hand-object reconstruction (SHOWMe, HOSt3R)
- ETH/MPI bimanual work (ARCTIC and the HANDS 2024/2025 challenge entries from several teams)
- The CTU-led BOP consortium (BOP 2023 and 2024 reports)
- Meta (HOT3D, NymeriaPlus), NVIDIA (HANDAL)
- Zhejiang (OnePose, OnePose++), HKU (Gen6D)
- PKU and Shanghai groups (Omni6DPose, Omni6D)
- TUM (HouseCat6D, PhoCaL), TU Wien (the Thalhammer T-RO survey and position paper)
- Robot-learning datasets (EgoVerse, HoloAssist, RoboTube, CosmoH2G)

Object-pose, HOI, body-object and robot-learning venues all report the same dependence on templates. The independent check I ran supports the core. Any6D (CVPR 2025, KAIST and NVIDIA) uses image-to-3D generation plus FoundationPose and reaches only 40.4 ADD and 38.3 AR on HO3D. Its authors say performance degrades when the initial shape is wrong because the method never updates the shape. That matches SHOWMe: F-score 37.6 with COLMAP registration versus 73.5 with ground-truth transforms. Bimanual template-free reconstruction remains weak in the HANDS challenge reports. No community has treated hand-held template-free pose and shape as solved.

Sub-claims that are partly artifacts or overstated:
1. The model-free 0.25 vs model-based 0.67 AR figure comes from one industrial dataset with textureless parts (IndustryShapes). On YCB-Video, FoundationPose model-free with 16 posed reference images reaches 97.4 ADD-S and 91.5 ADD AUC, and 99.9 ADD-0.1d on LINEMOD. Model-free pose from a static, well-posed reference capture is therefore close to solved on textured household objects. The gap is specific to industrial or textureless objects and to manipulation-style onboarding, not field-wide.
2. That the BOP 2024 model-free 6D track received no submissions is weak evidence. The track was new, the 2D model-free track did attract entries (for example GFreeDet), and the dynamic onboarding sequences for HOT3D and HANDAL were completed only in August 2025. It reflects the challenge's timing and organization as much as the difficulty of the task. I could not retrieve the BOP 2025 model-free results.
3. The category-level collapse from 62.52 to 14.42 percent 5deg2cm, and 3.24 percent on unseen categories, comes from one paper's large-vocabulary benchmark (Omni6D). Much of the community has since moved to model-free and generated-mesh approaches, so category scaling is a contested route rather than the field's main bottleneck.
4. Robot-learning datasets that release masks only are partly a matter of cost and convention. Several of these papers are arXiv 2026 and the corpus lists no authors for them. Recent pipelines do produce object poses with generated or scanned meshes plus FoundationPose.

Net: the evidence is broad, but the statement bundles narrow, dataset-specific numbers with the real problem. The real problem is joint pose and shape estimation when the only observation of the object is the occluded hand-manipulation video itself (textureless surfaces, bimanual grasps, regrasps), with no static clean capture and no shape refinement. Under that narrower wording the pain point survives this lens.

skeptics.reframe: Model-free 6D pose from a static, well-posed reference capture is close to solved on textured household objects (FoundationPose model-free reaches 97.4 ADD-S on YCB-Video). What remains open across communities is jointly estimating object shape and pose when the only observation of a new object is the hand-manipulation video itself: hands hide much of it, surfaces are textureless, both hands hold it, and grasps change. In that setting, current pipelines based on image-to-3D generated meshes or SfM fall to about 40 ADD on HO3D (Any6D) and about half the ground-truth-registration F-score on SHOWMe, and none of them refine the shape while tracking.

skeptics.reasons:
The skeptic case is partly true. Some of P02 is engineering or data effort. That datasets limit themselves to a few scanned objects, or release no object pose, is a resourcing and annotation choice. The category-level collapse on Omni6D (62.52 to 14.42 percent 5deg2cm, 3.24 on unseen categories) is fading as a research target, because the field is moving from category priors to model-free onboarding and generative shape priors. A recipe also exists that looks like the known solution waiting for resources: generate or scan a mesh (TRELLIS, SAM 3D Objects), then track it with FoundationPose. Recent work runs exactly this pipeline: AGILE, SIGGRAPH 2026, which uses VLM-guided generation and then tracking, and GRC-Pose, arXiv 2609.39116, which uses SAM3D CAD plus correspondence and reports SOTA on HOT3D.

The core is still not refuted. It holds a question that top-venue reviewers have repeatedly found significant: how to jointly estimate 6D pose and shape of an unseen object online, from one RGB or RGB-D stream, when hands hide most of its surface. Evidence that the question is live and publishable, not solved:
(1) Model-free FoundationPose scores 0.25 AR versus 0.67 with CAD on IndustryShapes.
(2) The BOP 2024 model-free hand-manipulation onboarding track drew no submissions.
(3) On SHOWMe, the F-score at 5 mm falls from 73.5 to 37.6 when COLMAP replaces ground-truth transforms.
(4) HOLD-style methods handle only one hand and fail in bimanual settings.
(5) Top venues keep accepting papers on it: Any6D (CVPR 2025, single RGB-D anchor, evaluated on HO3D), HOLD (CVPR 2024), AGILE (SIGGRAPH 2026). Arrivals in 2026 continue (ComPose 2605.23523, GRC-Pose 2609.39116).

The generative-prior recipe does not close the problem; it opens new questions. Generated geometry is guessed on exactly the hand-occluded surfaces, has unknown metric scale, and is not checked against observations. The pipelines are offline and assume a rigid grasp and a single hand. Reconciling a generated prior with partial sensor evidence, with bounded error, in real time and under bimanual occlusion and regrasping, is an open scientific question and not a matter of resources.

Risk for the author: the area is crowded and fast-moving, with three or more groups releasing SAM3D- and FoundationPose-based trackers in 2026. A contribution must target the residual gap (online, metric, uncertainty-aware, bimanual), not template-free tracking in general.

skeptics.reframe: Generative shape priors (SAM 3D, TRELLIS) now supply a mesh for any object, but they guess the hand-occluded surfaces, and their metric scale and pose are ambiguous. The open question: how to track the pose and refine the shape of an unseen object online from one RGB-D stream during bimanual manipulation and regrasping, reconciling the guessed geometry with partial depth and hand-contact evidence, and keeping pose error bounded and measurable rather than only offline and plausible-looking. Target: close the model-free versus model-based gap (0.25 vs 0.67 AR) on hand-manipulation benchmarks such as HOT3D and ARCTIC.

research_questions.question: RQ1 (strongest). When a generated mesh of a hand-occluded object (SAM 3D Objects or TRELLIS, made from one early frame) seeds an online RGB-D tracker, can the tracker keep a per-surface provenance field (seen in depth, hallucinated by the generator, hidden by a hand) and replace hallucinated geometry with measured geometry as it goes? Can it also weight pose refinement by that provenance, so that generator-guessed or hand-hidden surfaces never drive the 6D pose? Goal: close most of the gap between a frozen generated mesh and the ground-truth mesh during hand manipulation, at interactive rates.
research_questions.why_top_venue: Generate-then-track (SAM 3D or image-to-3D mesh, then FoundationPose) is now the default recipe, and its failure mode is documented by the people who built it. Any6D (CVPR 2025) states that it never updates the shape and degrades when the generated shape is wrong. On HO3D it reaches ADD-S 98.7 but only ADD 40.4. My reading, not a verified diagnosis: the poses are geometrically close but rotationally ambiguous, which wrong shape or texture would explain. HIPPo (arXiv 2502.10606, RGB-D, verified) already refines a diffusion-prior mesh online by replacing the prior with measurements. It updates in about 10 s per mesh, was tested only on static objects (YCB-Video, LM-O), and lists severe occlusion as a limitation it does not handle. GRC-Pose (arXiv 2609.39116, 30 Sep 2026) is RGB-only and does not refine the SAM3D CAD. Point2Pose (arXiv 2604.10415) builds a TSDF online but uses no generative prior and ignores hands. No verified work refines the shape of a generated prior online under hand occlusion with provenance-weighted pose. A clean, measurable fix to the field's standard pipeline on public hand-object RGB-D benchmarks fits CVPR/ICCV/ECCV, or ICRA/RA-L if real-time performance is the main selling point.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) Initialise: SAM2 object mask on the first frame, then SAM 3D Objects (or TRELLIS) mesh, then metric scale and pose from the depth by robust scale-ICP against the visible depth points. (2) Representation: the generated mesh converted to a surfel or 2D-Gaussian set (or a TSDF with a prior layer). Each element carries a provenance state {prior, observed, hand-hidden} and a confidence from observation count and depth residual. (3) Hand-aware free-space: hand masks from a hand-mesh estimator (HaMeR or WiLoR) plus SAM2. Depth pixels on the hand are marked unknown and are never used to carve or confirm object surface, so fingers do not erase the object and are not fused into it. (4) Pose: frozen pretrained FoundationPose refiner (render-and-compare), plus a depth-ICP term weighted by provenance confidence, so prior-only surfaces get low weight. Optional CoTracker-style 2D point tracks for drift. (5) Shape update in a background thread on keyframes: fuse newly observed depth, then decay prior elements contradicted by observation, i.e. visible free space where the prior predicts surface. Output the mesh with provenance colouring for the digital twin. (6) No large-scale training. At most a small learned confidence head, trained on DexYCB.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Four to six weeks, single GPU. On HO3D v3 (RGB-D, single hand) and the HO-Cap handover sequences (multi-view RGB-D, use one view), run three configurations: (a) FoundationPose tracking with a first-frame generated mesh, scale-aligned and frozen; (b) the same with the ground-truth mesh, as the oracle; (c) the proposed provenance-weighted online refinement. Report ADD, ADD-S and BOP AR per sequence, plus Chamfer and F-score at 5 mm on observed surfaces over time. Ablations: hand pixels treated as free space vs unknown; provenance weighting on vs off. Go/no-go: (c) recovers at least half of the ADD gap between (a) and (b), keeps pose at 10 Hz or more, and shape F-score rises with time. If (a) is already within a few points of (b), the premise fails and the direction should be dropped.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data: HO3D v3 (RGB-D, one hand, YCB objects), DexYCB (multi-view RGB-D, one hand), HO-Cap (multi-RGB-D plus HoloLens, includes handovers between hands, verified from its abstract), H2O (multi-view RGB-D, two hands with 6D object poses and meshes, verified from its abstract), YCBInEOAT (robot in-hand, RGB-D). ARCTIC and HOT3D have no depth. Use them only through rendered depth or Quest 3 stereo depth, and say so. Models: SAM2, SAM 3D Objects or TRELLIS, FoundationPose weights (NVIDIA non-commercial research licence), HaMeR or WiLoR, optional CoTracker3. Hardware: one workstation GPU with 24 GB (SAM 3D Objects peak memory not verified; TRELLIS is the fallback), a few hundred GB to about 1 TB of storage (per-dataset sizes not verified), one consumer RGB-D camera for qualitative in-the-wild demos. No mocap or robot needed.
research_questions.risks: (1) Speed of the field. GRC-Pose, ComPose, Point2Pose and EgoAERO appeared between April and September 2026, and NVIDIA or Meta could add shape updating to FoundationPose or SAM 3D within months. Scope the claim tightly to hand-occluded, provenance-aware, online. (2) HIPPo is the closest prior art. If its code is available, reviewers will require it as a baseline, and the novelty must rest on hand-aware carving and provenance-weighted pose, not on prior replacement in general. (3) The frozen FoundationPose refiner was trained on complete meshes and may not benefit from partial, provenance-coloured geometry without fine-tuning. (4) Ground-truth bias. HO-Cap and similar sets annotate poses semi-automatically, possibly with FoundationPose-like tools (not verified), which could favour FoundationPose-based trackers. (5) Consumer depth fails on small, thin, dark or specular objects, exactly the hard cases. (6) The BOP 2025 model-free results could not be verified. A stronger published baseline may already exist.

research_questions.question: RQ2. In bimanual manipulation with regrasps and handovers, can 3D hand pose and contact state work as a second sensor for an unscanned object, so that its 6D track survives the windows where too little object surface is visible for render-and-compare? The tracker would detect contact-change events (regrasp, handover) and switch which hand, if any, anchors the object. Every frame it would output an evidence type (measured from the object, carried by hand i, constrained by contact or support) with a pose covariance.
research_questions.why_top_venue: Hand-object methods still assume one hand and a fixed grasp. The P02 record and the skeptics agree that HOLD-style methods handle a single hand with near-constant contact and fail in bimanual settings. ComPose (arXiv 2605.23523, verified) uses hand joints as a complementary cue, but it is RGB-only and single-hand, with no switching across grasp changes. TwinTrack (ICRA 2026, verified) fuses contact physics for unknown objects, but with a robot hand whose kinematics are known. GHOST and Grasp in Gaussians are single-hand and offline. Robot learning from human video (EgoAERO, DexImit) needs object trajectories through handovers, and CosmoH2G reports 19.34 vs 10.27 deg orientation error when object pose is induced from the hand rather than tracked. No verified method does online, metric, model-free bimanual tracking through handovers with honest per-frame uncertainty. Strongest at ICRA, CoRL or RSS if a borrowed arm replays the demonstration; CVPR or ECCV if the vision contribution carries it.
research_questions.method_sketch: Build on the RQ1 tracker (or on FoundationPose with a generated mesh) as the object-evidence measurement. Hands: per-frame MANO meshes for both hands (HaMeR or WiLoR), placed metrically with depth. Contact: per-hand contact probability from the signed distance between hand vertices and the current object surface, plus agreement in relative motion over a short window. State estimation: a switching filter (IMM, or a sliding-window factor graph with GTSAM) with modes {free/visual, rigidly attached to left, rigidly attached to right, attached to both, resting on support}. In attached modes, the hand-to-object relative transform is a slowly varying latent that is re-estimated whenever enough of the object is visible. Mode switches are driven by the contact probabilities and by visual residuals. Output: pose, covariance, and evidence label per frame. Handover is modelled as a both-hands transition mode, not as track loss.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Three to five weeks. From HO-Cap handover sequences and H2O two-hand segments, compute the visible-object fraction for each frame from the GT mesh and pose, after occlusion by the GT hands. Compare object-only tracking (FoundationPose with generated mesh, frozen) against the switching tracker. Report ADD-0.1d recall binned by visible fraction (with the below-30 percent bin as the headline), track-loss count, recovery time after each handover, and the empirical coverage of the reported 2-sigma pose covariance. Go/no-go: clear gains in the low-visibility bins without losing accuracy in high-visibility frames, and coverage within about 5 points of nominal. As a small sanity check only, add the author's own recordings with an ArUco-marked object, with the marker masked so it gives no texture cue.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data: HO-Cap (handovers, RGB-D), H2O (two hands, RGB-D, 6D object poses), DexYCB and HO3D v3 for single-hand calibration of the contact model. ARCTIC (bimanual, articulated, RGB-only) only as a stress test with rendered depth, labelled as synthetic depth. Hardware: one GPU, one consumer RGB-D camera. A borrowed robot arm is optional, for a replay demo targeting CoRL/RSS. No mocap. Ground truth comes only from public datasets.
research_questions.risks: (1) Hand-mesh estimators are least accurate exactly when the object occludes the fingers, so the hand sensor fails in the same frames as the object sensor. The estimator has to model this correlation, or the covariance will be overconfident. (2) Public RGB-D bimanual data with object poses is small: H2O has few objects and HO-Cap has a limited number of handover clips (exact counts not verified). Results may be on a few dozen sequences, which reviewers may find thin. (3) Rigid-attachment modes break under in-hand sliding and rolling, and articulated objects (ARCTIC) violate rigidity. (4) A vision venue may see the switching filter as classical engineering. The contribution needs a clear learned or principled component, e.g. a contact estimator or a calibrated evidence model. (5) ComPose or a successor could add a bimanual extension quickly.

research_questions.question: RQ3 (cheapest; best folded into RQ1 or RQ2 rather than published alone). Can a model-free hand-held object tracker report a calibrated per-frame bound on its own pose error (rotation and translation), computed only from signals it already has: render-and-compare score, depth residual on observed versus prior surfaces, visible fraction, hand-contact state? Do these bounds keep their nominal coverage when moving from single-hand training data (DexYCB, HO3D) to bimanual handover data (HO-Cap, H2O)? Downstream consumers (a digital twin, a robot-learning pipeline that filters demonstrations) need to know which frames to trust.
research_questions.why_top_venue: Conformal confidence regions for 6D pose exist only in the model-based setting. Deterministic Object Pose Confidence Region Estimation (ICCV 2025, verified) uses CAD keypoints on LM-O and SPEED. EgoAERO introduces an online quality-assessment mechanism for asset-free tracking, but I could not verify whether it is calibrated. The skeptics' reframe asks for pose error that is bounded and measurable, not merely plausible. Calibrated, distribution-shift-tested error bounds for template-free tracking under hand occlusion are not verified anywhere. Alone this is probably RA-L or ICRA level. As the uncertainty layer of RQ1 or RQ2 it lifts either one toward CVPR or CoRL.
research_questions.method_sketch: Wrap two or three existing model-free trackers: FoundationPose with a generated mesh, BundleSDF, and Point2Pose if its code is released. Log per-frame features: refiner score, depth residual split by provenance, visible fraction, mask IoU change, hand-contact probability, frames since last high-visibility observation. Train a small error regressor (gradient-boosted trees or an MLP) on DexYCB and HO3D. Calibrate with split conformal prediction, adding an adaptive or weighted variant for temporal dependence and shift. Evaluate coverage and bound tightness on HO-Cap and H2O.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Two to three weeks, if RQ1 or RQ2 logging already exists. Report coverage at 80, 90 and 95 percent nominal, mean bound width compared with a constant-bound baseline and with the raw refiner score thresholded, and coverage stratified by visible fraction and by handover windows. Go/no-go: coverage within about 5 points of nominal under shift, with bounds clearly tighter than the constant baseline in high-visibility frames.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Same public RGB-D datasets as RQ1 and RQ2 (DexYCB, HO3D v3, HO-Cap, H2O). Runs on CPU plus one GPU for tracker inference. No new capture needed.
research_questions.risks: (1) Calibration is a thin standalone contribution, and reviewers may call it incremental over ICCV 2025 conformal pose work. (2) Temporal correlation and dataset shift can break exchangeability, so naive conformal will under-cover on bimanual data. That is itself a finding, but it weakens the claim. (3) Bounds may come out too wide to be useful in the low-visibility frames where they matter most.
target_venues: CVPR (only combined with RQ1 or RQ2)

fit.thesis_assets_help: Small. They do not change the go/no-go call. Where they help: (1) the causal 30 fps RGB-D chain on one desk setup is a ready base for the online tracker in RQ1 and RQ2 and saves a few weeks of engineering; (2) the measured/held/constrained honesty labels are close to the per-frame evidence type and calibrated uncertainty in RQ2 and RQ3, so they offer a conceptual seed and a thesis-to-paper link, though not evidence; (3) the object-conditioned recovery of an occluded holding arm is the reverse direction (arm from object), and its contact and attachment logic could be inverted for the hand-anchored modes of RQ2; (4) the ArUco-marked object gives metric ground truth for a held object on the author's own recordings, but only as a sanity check: the marker adds texture that makes model-free tracking easier, so it must be masked or inpainted before evaluation; (5) the Unity twin is useful only for demo videos. Limits: 28 recordings of one subject with one marked object cannot serve as a top-venue evaluation set. All headline numbers must come from public RGB-D benchmarks (HO3D v3, DexYCB, HO-Cap, H2O). The assets are not a competitive edge against the NVIDIA, Meta, ETH, MPI, MIT and TUM groups working on this problem.
fit.what_a_small_lab_cannot_do_here: Five things are out of reach. (1) Train or substantially retrain foundation components: image-to-3D generators (SAM 3D, TRELLIS), FoundationPose-scale pose refiners trained on millions of synthetic renders, or feed-forward hand-object reconstructors such as ForeHOI, HORT and Object Pose Transformer, which need large synthetic datasets and multi-GPU clusters. The lab must use these frozen and contribute the online, provenance and uncertainty layer around them. (2) Build a new benchmark with mocap-grade ground truth for many unscanned objects in bimanual manipulation. Without multi-view rigs, mocap or scanners, it depends on HO-Cap, H2O, DexYCB and HO3D, which are small for bimanual RGB-D. (3) Compete on generic template-free hand-object reconstruction from RGB video (the BIGS, MagicHOI, GHOST, Grasp in Gaussians, HOSt3R, CARI4D line) or on generic model-free 6D pose (Any6D, PANY, GRC-Pose). That space is crowded and moves monthly. (4) Make strong in-the-wild RGB-only generalisation claims or run large-scale evaluation such as BOP-H3 with HOT3D, which has no depth. (5) Show robot-learning gains without at least a borrowed arm, which limits the CoRL and RSS angle to replay or simulation demos. Note also that the web search budget ran out during this analysis; the BOP 2025 model-free results and the closest 2026 competitors beyond those listed (HIPPo, GRC-Pose, ComPose, Point2Pose, TwinTrack, EgoAERO) need one more targeted check before the lab commits.

painpoint.name: Accuracy only offline: no causal real-time estimate

evidence.latest_state: Fast methods now exist for each part of the problem, but no 2025-2026 paper I found shows a strictly causal joint hand-object or body-object tracker that matches offline accuracy under heavy occlusion. Unseen-object 6D estimation is still a trade between accuracy and speed. The BOP Challenge 2024 report (arXiv 2504.02812) gives the best unseen-object method, FreeZeV2.1, 22% more accuracy than GenFlow on BOP-Classic-Core, but at 24.9 s per image against 2.7 s for the best seen-object method. Co-op (CVPR 2025) takes 0.8 s per image and is only 13% more accurate than GenFlow. Unseen-object pose tracking from RGB-D got much faster in 2026. RRTrack (arXiv 2607.23669) reports 55.2 FPS and a 66.3% gain in ADD-S AR over FoundationPose on its own synthetic dynamic benchmark. An RA-L 2026 tracker (arXiv 2607.23468) runs at 57.6 FPS with failure detection and recovery, and matches state-of-the-art accuracy only on easy sequences. Both still need a CAD model or template and are scored on their own occlusion sets. For monocular human-object interaction, THO (arXiv 2603.14435, March 2026) is a feed-forward spatial-temporal transformer at 31.5 FPS on one RTX 4090. It claims a speedup of more than 600x over optimisation-based methods such as VisTracker, with better Chamfer distance and acceleration on BEHAVE and InterCap. It needs an object template, and whether its temporal window uses future frames is not stated. For hands, HandFlow (arXiv 2607.11221) reconstructs 150-frame sequences at 47 fps and cuts world-space error by more than 30% on DexYCB and HOT3D. It works on a whole sequence window, so it is fast but not shown to be causal. No 2025-2026 challenge report I found sets a latency budget for UmeTrack, HOT3D or RHOBIN, so the gap the pain point describes (accuracy only after offline smoothing) still holds at benchmark level.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: End-to-End Spatial-Temporal Transformer for Real-time 4D HOI Reconstruction (THO)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Feed-forward monocular human-object 4D reconstruction from video plus a 3D template, using contact-proximity spatial priors and temporal kinematic priors. Runs at 31.5 FPS on an RTX 4090, claims a speedup of more than 600x over optimisation-based methods, and reports better accuracy and smoothness on BEHAVE and InterCap. Whether it is causal is not stated.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: HandFlow: Fully Generative 4D Hand Recovery with Flow Matching
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Flow-matching generative prior over hand motion sequences that replaces per-frame regressors. Reconstructs 150-frame windows at 47 fps, about 12x faster than earlier video methods, and cuts world-space pose error by more than 30% on DexYCB and HOT3D. It processes whole windows, so it is not shown to be causal.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: RRTrack: Robust and Recoverable Object 6D Pose Tracking for Dynamic Scenes
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Training-free 2D-6D closed-loop tracking that couples video object segmentation, DINOv2 template matching and pose refinement. Runs at 55.2 FPS and reports a 66.3% improvement in ADD-S AR over FoundationPose on a new synthetic benchmark with fast motion and occlusion.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Robust 6-DoF Object Pose Tracking with Built-In Recovery under Occlusions and Rapid Object Motions
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Model-based RGB-D tracking of unseen objects that combines learned keypoint matching, optimisation-based alignment, failure detection and global re-detection. Runs at 57.6 FPS, matches state-of-the-art accuracy on easy sequences and is the most robust on a new dataset of occluded, fast-moving scenes.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: BOP Challenge 2024 on Model-Based and Model-Free 6D Object Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Benchmark report that quantifies the accuracy-speed gap for unseen objects: FreeZeV2.1 at 24.9 s per image is the most accurate, Co-op at 0.8 s per image is the practical alternative, seen objects take 2.7 s, and 2D detection of unseen objects is the main bottleneck.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Co-op: Correspondence-based Novel Object Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Correspondence-based estimator for novel-object pose. The BOP 2024 report gives it 0.8 s per image and 13% more accuracy than GenFlow, though it stays below FreeZeV2.1.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: RGBTrack: Fast, Robust Depth-Free 6D Pose Estimation and Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Real-time RGB-only pose estimation and tracking built on FoundationPose, adding binary-search depth, render-and-compare, XMem 2D tracking, a Kalman filter and a state machine for occlusion. The abstract gives no FPS or accuracy figures.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: GRC-Pose: Generation-Reconstruction Correspondence for Prior-Free 6D Object Pose Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: CAD-free 6D object pose tracking from a single RGB video. Claims state-of-the-art AR on HOT3D and a 58% gain in motion retention. Runtime and causality not checked.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: OMNI-PoseX: A Fast Vision Model for 6D Object Pose Estimation in Embodied Tasks
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Open-vocabulary 6D pose foundation model with an SO(3)-aware flow-matching rotation predictor. Claims state-of-the-art accuracy at real-time speed for grasping unseen objects. The abstract gives no numbers.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: AVI-HT: Adaptive Vision-IMU Fusion for 3D Hand Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Fuses egocentric vision with IMUs on a glove for hand tracking, cutting mean keypoint error by 16.1% on DexGloveHOI. This sidesteps visual occlusion with extra sensors. Runtime not checked.

evidence.crowdedness: MEDIUM: at least ten 2025-2026 papers attack speed, but most are robotics object-pose trackers (RA-L, IROS and arXiv groups) or hand-only and HOI-only feed-forward models; very few attack causal joint hand-object or bimanual tracking at offline-level accuracy, and no benchmark sets a latency budget.
evidence.trend: rising: during 2026 several real-time feed-forward replacements for optimisation pipelines appeared (THO at 31.5 FPS for HOI, HandFlow at 47 fps, RRTrack and the RA-L recovery tracker at 55-58 FPS), driven by robot demonstration capture and embodied manipulation that need live estimates.

skeptics.reasons:
Not refuted, but the "speed" half of P03 is being solved and the claim needs narrowing. Web search was unavailable (the shared budget was used up), so the evidence comes from WebFetch of the arXiv API, arXiv abstract pages and the BOP leaderboard.

(1) Throughput is no longer the barrier for several sub-problems. THO (arXiv 2603.14435, Mar 2026) reconstructs monocular 4D human-object interaction feed-forward at 31.5 FPS on an RTX 4090. It reports a >600x speedup over optimisation baselines, along with better accuracy and temporal consistency. That undercuts the CHORE ~312 s per frame item. HandFlow (arXiv 2607.11221, Jul 2026) reconstructs a 150-frame hand sequence at 47 fps, about 12x faster than prior video methods, with over 30 percent lower world-space error and the lowest acceleration error. This means offline smoothing is no longer required for temporal stability. For unseen-object 6D, the BOP Classic-Core leaderboard now lists WAPR.v2.1 (MUSE) at 0.806 AR in 0.72 s per image, against a best of 0.845 AR at 50-213 s. The accuracy gap at sub-second speed is now about 4 AR points, not the 24.9 s versus 3.87 s trade-off in the record. FoundationPose's tracking mode (CVPR 2024) already runs at roughly 30 Hz after initialisation, so 'unseen-object estimators below 4 FPS' mixes up per-image estimation with video tracking. Several 2025-2026 works report real-time unseen or novel-object 6D: 2510.11687 at 28 FPS, plus HRC-Pose and OMNI-PoseX, whose accuracy against BOP leaders is not verified.

(2) What survives is causality and latency, not FPS. THO uses a window of future frames and HandFlow processes a whole 150-frame clip. Both are fast but non-causal, so they still cannot drive a robot reacting during a handover, sub-frame-latency contact (the bathing case) or live AR. I found no 2025-2026 causal per-frame method that matches offline accuracy under heavy hand-object or body-object occlusion. The BOP leaderboard has no latency-constrained track, and the record says hand challenges rank offline-smoothed results. Products such as headset hand tracking are causal and real-time, but the challenge numbers show a roughly 4 mm MPJPE gap (17.91 mm causal versus 13.92 mm smoothed), and they do not estimate object pose or contact.

(3) Parts of the record are dated. Rerun the evidence items for CHORE, FoundationPose FPS and FreeZe timing against 2026 entries before using them as motivation.

skeptics.reframe: Throughput is no longer the gap: feed-forward HOI and hand reconstruction now runs at 30-47 FPS, and unseen-object 6D at 0.7 s per image is within about 4 AR points of the leaders. The open problem is a strictly causal, low-latency (no future frames, around one frame of delay) estimate of hand, body and object pose and contact under heavy occlusion that matches window or offline accuracy. No benchmark scores accuracy under a latency budget, so live uses (handover reaction, contact-rich assistance, AR feedback) stay blocked.

skeptics.reasons:
P03 as stated ("no causal method of comparable accuracy runs in real time" across hand, hand-object, human-object and unseen-object pose) holds up only in part. Most of its support comes from the conventions of particular setups, and some of the field has long treated real-time causal tracking as solved.

(1) Pooling artifact. About 15 of the 58 papers are dataset papers describing their own offline ground-truth pipelines, where offline is the design choice and not a limitation of the field: HiSC4D, HSC4D, SLOPER4D, NeuralDome, InterCap, HOI-M3, Hi4D, HUMOTO, WorldPose and AddBiomechanics. About 10 more are face, head or avatar capture papers outside hand-object tracking: Multiface, NeRSemble, HumanRF/ActorsHQ, HumanOLAT, Codec Avatar Studio (listed twice, ids 438 and 1430), SmartPortraits and an avatar survey. The 1 GPU-day per sequence (SHOWMe/HHOR) and 312 s per frame (CHORE in the RHOBIN report) figures describe template-free reconstruction and early optimisation baselines, not the best that exists.

(2) Single-protocol artifact for object pose. The "24.9 s per image" and "FoundationPose 0.98 FPS" figures come from the BOP single-image, from-scratch localisation protocol. In tracking mode, FoundationPose (CVPR 2024, verified from the arXiv HTML) runs at about 32 Hz and reaches 93.09 ADD AUC on YCBInEOAT and 96.0 on YCB-Video. That is causal, real-time and the most accurate result reported there. The robotics tracking community has run real-time for years: ICG (CVPR 2022) takes 1.3 ms per frame on one CPU core, and BundleSDF (CVPR 2023) is near-real-time for unknown objects.

(3) Real-time hand and hand-object tracking exists in other communities. UmeTrack (SIGGRAPH Asia 2022) runs in real-time VR products. WiLoR (CVPR 2025) includes a real-time localisation stage. Sridhar et al. (ECCV 2016) did real-time joint hand-object tracking from one RGB-D camera.

(4) The pain point's own evidence shows a small offline-versus-causal gap for hands. Offline smoothing improves UmeTrack MPJPE from 17.91 to 13.92 mm (1530), and per 1531, smoothing plus optimisation adds only 0.5 AUC. The headline challenge gaps come from post-hoc smoothing that challenge entrants add to win leaderboards, a convention of the HANDS workshop reports (1528-1532, 1543, 1547), not a fundamental barrier.

(5) The "blocked application" evidence is a handful of robotics dataset papers: ATTACH (1189), handover failure detection (1165) and robot-assisted bathing (697). Each uses a different setup, so the groups are diverse, but none measures a causal-versus-offline accuracy gap. The diversity of groups is real (Meta, MPI, NVIDIA, CMU, ShanghaiTech, TU Munich and others), so this is not one lab's quirk. The general statement is still an overclaim built from mixed-purpose papers.

What survives is narrower. There is no paired, latency-budgeted evaluation for jointly tracking hands, or a body, together with an object through contact and heavy occlusion. The components are real-time on their own: rigid-object tracking, and hand tracking that is free of occlusion or uses multiple views. The joint, contact-consistent setting is reported mainly offline, and HOI benchmarks (ARCTIC, HOT3D, BEHAVE/RHOBIN, DexYCB) report no runtime or causality constraint. BOP does report runtime, which is a counterexample.

Verification limits: the web search budget ran out after the first few checks, so the claims about counterexamples rest on the abstract and HTML fetches cited in the evidence list.

skeptics.reframe: Real-time causal trackers exist for each part on its own: rigid objects (FoundationPose tracking at about 32 Hz, ICG) and hands (UmeTrack). What is missing is a latency-budgeted, causal evaluation, and a method, for jointly tracking hands (or a body) and an object through contact and heavy occlusion from one RGB-D or monocular camera. HOI benchmarks such as ARCTIC, HOT3D, DexYCB and BEHAVE/RHOBIN report no runtime or causality constraint, so the best reported joint hand-object and human-object results come from offline smoothing or optimisation. How large the causal-versus-offline gap is in this joint setting has never been measured.

skeptics.reasons:
As written, most of P03 does not hold up as a research question. It merges four different complaints. (a) BOP unseen-object 6D localisation takes 24.9 s per image, and FoundationPose pose estimation runs at 0.98 FPS. (b) Avatar and clinical pipelines fit each subject or trial offline. (c) Challenge entries apply a Savitzky-Golay or Neural Smooth filter after the fact. (d) HHOR camera refinement costs about one GPU-day per sequence. Items (a), (b) and (d) are mostly speed problems with known remedies: distillation, fewer pose hypotheses, lightweight networks, faster hardware, or initialising once and then tracking. The record itself says these fixes trade accuracy for speed or are still proposals. That is the "solution known, waiting for resources" case, so this part is refuted.

One question survives and has precedent at top venues. Can a causal estimator with a fixed latency budget match offline whole-sequence accuracy for hands and hand-object pose under heavy occlusion? Today occlusion and depth ambiguity are resolved by looking at future frames and iterating render-and-compare. The evidence measures this gap: 13.92 mm MPJPE with offline smoothing against 17.91 mm without it on UmeTrack (paper 1530), and the cobot detector that depends on future frames (1189). This is a modelling and learning question, not an engineering one. It asks what information future frames supply and whether a learned persistent state, motion and contact priors, or physics can replace it causally. It also asks how to report delay-versus-accuracy trade-offs, a separate open question.

Precedents (checked on arXiv this session, venues from my knowledge):
- WHAM (CVPR 2024) was published because it made world-grounded body motion online and efficient, where the most accurate methods needed offline optimisation.
- CUT3R (2025) puts a stateful recurrent model behind streaming 3D reconstruction.
- BundleSDF (CVPR 2023) tracks and reconstructs unknown objects online at near real-time.
Reviewers therefore accept "close the gap between online and offline accuracy" as a contribution. It is also not saturated for hand-object: an arXiv abstract search for online real-time hand-object reconstruction returned nothing relevant. A search can miss work, so this is weak evidence.

Caveats: the web-search budget was used up, so several 2025-2026 streaming hand-object papers may exist that I could not check. A reviewer will reject a paper that only offers a faster network at slightly lower accuracy. The publishable version needs a principled causal mechanism, such as state, priors or physics, or a protocol that scores latency, or both.
