skeptics.reframe: Under bimanual and hand-object occlusion, how much of the accuracy that offline whole-sequence methods gain from future frames can a causal estimator with fixed latency recover, using a learned persistent state, contact or physics priors, and RGB-D? How should the delay-versus-accuracy trade-off be measured (for example 13.92 vs 17.91 mm MPJPE on UmeTrack with and without offline smoothing) so that methods are ranked under a latency budget rather than by offline accuracy alone? Raw speed-ups such as distillation or lighter networks for unseen-object 6D or for avatars do not count as the research question.

fit.worth_pursuing: MAYBE. It is worth pursuing only in its narrowed form, and only with a go/no-go pilot. The narrowed form is strictly causal, low-latency joint tracking of hand(s) and object through contact and heavy occlusion, plus a protocol that scores it under a latency budget. Raw speed is being solved quickly by others: THO at 31.5 FPS, though bidirectional over a 64-frame window (checked in the arXiv HTML); InfiniHand (arXiv 2609.35743, Sep 2026), hand-only streaming at 11.19 FPS; QORT-Former (AAAI 2025), per-frame two hands plus object at 53.5 FPS on H2O; and RRTrack and the RA-L 2026 tracker, object-only at 55-58 FPS. A paper that is only faster will be rejected. The open part has these pieces: (a) no one has measured the causal-versus-offline gap for joint hand-object tracking, and no HOI benchmark (DexYCB, HO3D, H2O, ARCTIC, HOT3D, BEHAVE) scores causality or latency; (b) arXiv API searches on 2026-10-02 found no causal joint hand-object tracker with persistent state that claims offline-level accuracy under occlusion (absence evidence, weak); and (c) the streaming-perception precedent (Li, Wang, Ramanan, ECCV 2020 oral) shows that latency-aware evaluation is accepted at top venues. Main risk: the gap may be small. Challenge reports show offline smoothing adding only 0.5 AUC, or 17.91 to 13.92 mm MPJPE, for hands alone. Measure the gap in months 1-2 and pivot if the heavy-occlusion gap is minor.

research_questions.question: RQ1 (measurement and protocol): In joint hand-object and bimanual 3D tracking, how large is the accuracy gap between causal estimators (no future frames, about one frame of latency) and offline ones (whole-window, bidirectional or smoothed)? In which frames does it arise: occlusion onset and re-emergence, grasp onset and release, fast motion? And does ranking methods under a latency budget change their order?
research_questions.why_top_venue: No HOI benchmark (DexYCB, HO3D, H2O, ARCTIC, HOT3D, BEHAVE/RHOBIN) scores causality or latency, and the BOP reports (2020-2024 abstracts checked) have runtime but no tracking track. Latency-aware evaluation already has a top-venue precedent: Towards Streaming Perception (ECCV 2020 oral) showed that streaming accuracy reorders 2D detectors. No 3D hand-object equivalent exists. The pain point's central claim is that accuracy is only available offline, and it has never been quantified in the joint setting; the artifact skeptic states this explicitly. A per-stratum measurement of what future frames contribute is a reusable finding that other groups would cite and build on.
research_questions.method_sketch: Define two complementary protocols. (1) Algorithmic lookahead: run each method with its temporal context masked to k future frames, k in {0, 1, 4, 16, full}, and score every frame t with the estimate available at t+k. (2) Wall-clock streaming in the style of Li et al.: replay video at 30 fps with measured per-frame runtime on a fixed reference GPU, and score each frame against the latest finished output. Metrics: hand MPJPE and MRRPE, object ADD-S and Chamfer, hand-relative object pose error, contact precision/recall and penetration, acceleration/jitter, and a new recovery-time-after-occlusion metric. Stratify by occlusion ratio, computed by rendering GT meshes for visible-pixel fractions, and by contact phase (approach, grasp onset, stable grasp, release). Method families: per-frame (WiLoR or HaMeR hands plus FoundationPose tracking; QORT-Former where code exists), causal filters on per-frame outputs (One Euro, Kalman), and window or offline methods with future masking (THO-style bidirectional transformer if code is released, HandFlow-style windows, optimisation fitting with smoothing).
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Three datasets: DexYCB (RGB-D), HO3D v3 (RGB-D) and H2O (egocentric RGB-D, two hands); add ARCTIC as RGB-only for articulated bimanual. Four to six methods across the families above. The headline figure is accuracy versus lookahead k for each occlusion and contact stratum, plus a table of how method ranks change under the wall-clock protocol. Go/no-go at month 2: if the heavy-occlusion stratum shows more than about 15-20 percent relative error reduction from full lookahead over k=0 (several mm hand error or several ADD-S AUC points), proceed to RQ2. Otherwise write it up as an analysis paper showing the gap is small and pivot.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data only: DexYCB, HO3D v3, H2O, ARCTIC, and optionally HOT3D. One 24 GB GPU is enough because the work is inference and masked re-runs of existing models. No capture, no mocap, no robot. Effort: about 2-3 student-months.
research_questions.risks: (1) The gap may be small: for hands alone, offline smoothing adds only 0.5 AUC in one UmeTrack challenge report, a 4 mm MPJPE gap in another. (2) A benchmark-only paper rarely gets into the CVPR main track, so pair it with RQ2 or send it to NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks. (3) Masking future frames in a model trained bidirectionally is unfair to that model. Retrain or fine-tune causal variants where feasible and state the caveat. (4) Some offline baselines have no public code. (5) Wall-clock numbers depend on hardware, so report the reference GPU and the algorithmic lookahead protocol separately. (6) Meta (HOT3D/UmeTrack organisers) could add an online track first.

research_questions.question: RQ2 (method): Can a causal estimator recover most of the offline accuracy when jointly tracking hand(s) and a rigid object through heavy mutual occlusion from one RGB-D camera, at no more than one frame of latency? It would use a learned persistent state with an explicit grasp-locked hand-object relative transform and contact state, updated by one causal depth render-and-compare step per frame, and distilled from an offline bidirectional teacher.
research_questions.why_top_venue: Reviewers accept closing the gap between online and offline accuracy as a contribution when the mechanism is principled: WHAM (CVPR 2024) made world-grounded body motion online; CUT3R (2025) streams 3D reconstruction with a persistent state; BundleSDF (CVPR 2023) tracks unknown objects online. In hand-object tracking, the 2026 fast methods are either non-causal windows (THO, HandFlow), hand-only (InfiniHand, AVI-HT, which needs an IMU glove), object-only (RRTrack, the RA-L 2026 tracker) or per-frame without temporal state (QORT-Former). The idea that future frames supply mainly grasp-consistency evidence, and that this evidence can be held causally, is testable and new to this setting.
research_questions.method_sketch: Frozen per-frame observers: a hand regressor (WiLoR or HaMeR), streaming masks (SAM2), an RGB-D object tracker (FoundationPose tracking mode, or ICG for a CPU fallback), and the depth map. A causal state model (GRU, Mamba, or a transformer with a causal mask) carries hand pose(s), object pose, the hand-to-object relative transform, a contact/grasp-phase variable and per-entity uncertainty. At each frame it predicts, then corrects with one differentiable render-and-compare step against observed depth and masks, so no iterative optimisation is needed. During a stable grasp, the visible entity propagates the occluded one through the locked relative transform; the state learns to detect grasp onset and release. Training: (a) GT supervision on DexYCB, HO3D and H2O; (b) distillation from an offline bidirectional teacher run on the same sequences, so the student learns what future frames would reveal; (c) an auxiliary task predicting the pose at t+k; (d) synthetic occlusion augmentation using mask pasting, to enrich the heavy-occlusion stratum. Output per-entity provenance labels (observed, propagated through grasp, prior-only) with calibrated uncertainty, so downstream users know which estimates are measured.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Train on DexYCB plus HO3D, then H2O for two hands. Evaluate with the RQ1 protocols against per-frame, causal-filter and offline baselines. Report the share of the offline-minus-causal gap that is closed overall and in the heavy-occlusion stratum, and the runtime: target 30 FPS or better at 640x480 on one consumer GPU, with the latency breakdown. Ablations: no grasp-lock state, no depth correction step, no teacher distillation, no future-prediction loss, and a Kalman/One Euro filter on the same per-frame inputs. That last ablation is the baseline reviewers will ask for. Calibration of the provenance labels, e.g. expected calibration error of uncertainty versus error. Cross-dataset test on HOT3D or ARCTIC (RGB only, with depth dropped) for generalisation. A live qualitative demo on a consumer RGB-D camera.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: DexYCB, HO3D v3 and H2O for training and evaluation; ARCTIC and HOT3D for cross-dataset tests. One 24-48 GB GPU, enough because the backbones are frozen and only the state model and correction step are trained. One consumer RGB-D camera, for the demo only. Object CAD models are required, as in DexYCB, HO3D and H2O. About 6-9 student-months after RQ1.
research_questions.risks: (1) Reviewers may call the learned state a Kalman filter; it must clearly beat strong filter baselines in the heavy-occlusion stratum, not just reduce jitter. (2) Errors in the frozen components (hand regressor under occlusion, object tracker drift) may dominate and limit the achievable gain. (3) The method is model-based; a CAD-free version would need online object modelling (BundleSDF-class compute), which is not real-time on one GPU. (4) Heavy-occlusion frames are a minority in DexYCB and HO3D, so headline averages can hide the effect. Report per-stratum results and use H2O, ARCTIC and HOT3D. (5) Strong competition: NVIDIA (FoundationPose/BundleSDF group) or Meta (HOT3D/UmeTrack) could release a causal joint tracker within the 12-18 months. (6) The teacher must be clearly better than the student's per-frame inputs, or distillation adds nothing; this is checked by RQ1.

research_questions.question: RQ3 (optional, downstream validation): For human-to-robot handover, does a causal tracker's accuracy, latency and calibrated uncertainty predict task success better than its offline accuracy does? Test this in simulation with HandoverSim on DexYCB motions, and on recorded multi-view RGB-D handovers from HOH, without a physical robot.
research_questions.why_top_venue: The pain point names handover reaction as the blocked application, but no paper links perception latency or causality to handover outcome. HandoverSim (ICRA 2022) and GenH2R (CVPR 2024) give a public closed-loop testbed, and HOH (NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks; multi-view RGB-D, fused point clouds, 2,720 handovers, 40 participants) gives real RGB-D handover sequences. Showing that rank under a latency budget predicts downstream success, while offline rank does not, would give RQ1's protocol a reason to exist and suits robotics venues.
research_questions.method_sketch: In HandoverSim, feed the receiving policy estimated hand and object states instead of privileged ones: per-frame, causal RQ2, and offline variants forced to wait k frames. Inject the measured latencies. Use a pose-conditioned receiver policy, or the benchmark's point-cloud policy with masks derived from the estimated poses. Measure success rate, hand-contact (safety) violations and time to grasp. On HOH, evaluate tracking quality in the transfer phase, where two hands occlude the object, using the dataset's provided annotations; whether they are accurate enough as ground truth is unverified. Use the per-entity provenance labels from RQ2 to gate the robot's action (wait while the estimate is prior-only) and measure the effect on safety violations.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: HandoverSim: three perception variants x four latency/lookahead settings x the standard test split, giving success and safety-violation curves, plus a rank-correlation analysis between RQ1 metrics and handover success. HOH: transfer-phase tracking accuracy for the same variants, if its annotations are adequate.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: HandoverSim (DexYCB motions, simulated) and HOH (public multi-view RGB-D). One GPU. No robot is needed; a borrowed arm would only be for an optional real-world demo.
research_questions.risks: (1) How HandoverSim's policy interfaces accept external perception is not verified; the GenH2R and GA-DDPG policies consume point clouds, so plugging in estimated poses may need policy retraining. (2) The success metric may not be sensitive to the latency range studied, a possible null result. (3) Results are sim-to-real limited. (4) HOH ground-truth quality for object and hand pose is unverified. (5) This RQ adds scope; treat it as a section of RQ2 or a follow-up ICRA paper, not a third main project.

fit.thesis_assets_help: A small edge, mostly conceptual, plus a live demo. (1) The object-conditioned recovery of an occluded holding arm is, in miniature, the grasp-locked state in RQ2: the visible object carries the occluded limb. It is a working prototype of the core mechanism and a head start on design intuition. (2) The measured/held/constrained honesty labels map directly onto RQ2's per-entity provenance output (observed, propagated through grasp, prior-only). This could be a distinctive, reviewable contribution if the labels are made calibrated. (3) The causal 30 fps chain and the author's measured offline-versus-causal smoother comparison show the author already measures latency against accuracy, and they give a ready live-demo path. Per knowledge/experiments.md and knowledge/transport_facts.md: about 28.7 fps sustained, transport p99 10.65 ms; on one wrist, causal Butterworth lag 142 ms versus One Euro 85 ms. (4) The ArUco-marked object with metric pose gives cheap object ground truth for a small real-world qualitative or sanity test. The assets do not provide benchmark evidence: the 28 recordings of one subject have no hand or arm ground truth (no mocap), cover one desk scene, and track the body or arm, not the hand mesh, so they cannot replace DexYCB, HO3D, H2O or ARCTIC in any table. The Unity twin is useful for a demo video and has little value for a venue.
fit.what_a_small_lab_cannot_do_here: The lab cannot build a new heavy-occlusion bimanual RGB-D benchmark with trustworthy hand and object ground truth: that needs mocap or a multi-view dome, as in DexYCB, ARCTIC and HOT3D. It also cannot pretrain foundation-scale streaming models: InfiniHand pretrains on about 5,000 hours of egocentric data, and THO-class HOI transformers need large GPU budgets. It cannot out-engineer industry on raw speed or on-device latency (UmeTrack in VR products, FoundationPose/ICG-class object trackers), or measure latency on headset hardware. Real-time template-free (CAD-free) online object modelling under hand occlusion, at BundleSDF-class compute, is out of reach on one GPU at 30 fps. Physical human-robot handover studies need a robot arm, a safety setup and ethics approval. Some offline baselines have no public code and would have to be reimplemented. Throughout, the lab should build on frozen public backbones and public datasets and contribute the protocol, the gap measurement and the causal state mechanism.

painpoint.name: Pose of the handled object during manipulation

evidence.latest_state: Accuracy on hand-held objects is still far below the level methods reach on static or camera-only-motion scenes. On HOT3D, GRC-Pose (arXiv 2609.39116, Sep 2026) is the newest prior-free RGB tracker. It reports state-of-the-art Average Recall of only 34.0 percent and motion retention of 26.9 percent, against Dynhor 31.9/17.0 and GigaPose 31.4/11.9. That is about the same one-third level that HOT3D reported for FoundPose with ground-truth masks (25.2 single-view, 33.8 multi-view). WHOLE (arXiv 2602.22209, Feb 2026) uses object templates plus a generative hand-object motion prior. On HOT3D-CLIP it reaches ADD/ADD-S AUC of 51.1/69.9, against 36.1/51.9 for FoundationPose. This is the largest verified jump, but it is a curated subset with known templates. ComPose (arXiv 2605.23523, May 2026) uses the hand as a complementary cue for RGB tracking. On DexYCB S3 it reports relative rotation error 1.5 deg and absolute rotation error 19.5 deg (MegaPose 62.6 deg). On HO-3D v2 its relative rotation error is 2.4 deg, against 33.4 deg for FoundPose. The 19.5 deg absolute error shows the problem is not closed. HOPformer (ECCV 2026, arXiv 2606.30598) reports 82.4 percent success on ARCTIC (+6.2 points) and introduces EPIC-Contact for in-the-wild egocentric hand-object pose. On the BOP side, the BOP 2024 report introduced BOP-H3, and the BOP 2025 challenge keeps the H3 tracks. I could not verify any published 2025 H3 accuracy that closes the gap to BOP-Classic-Core (50.4 AP). Body-object work in 2026, such as RePHO (CVPR 2026) and HA-HOI, targets physical plausibility rather than object pose error; I found no verified 2025-2026 result that brings BEHAVE or InterCap object error close to body error. Robot-side work (TwinTrack ICRA 2026, KineFuse IROS 2026) adds contact physics or haptics because vision alone fails under finger occlusion.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: GRC-Pose: Generation-Reconstruction Correspondence for Prior-Free 6D Object Pose Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Prior-free RGB 6D tracking using SAM3D-generated CAD and object-scene correspondences with posterior-gated memory through occlusion. HOT3D AR 34.0 and motion retention 26.9, against Dynhor 31.9/17.0. Names severe hand occlusion and intermittent visibility as the causes of drift.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: WHOLE: World-Grounded Hand-Object Lifted from Egocentric Videos
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Generative hand-object motion prior guided by egocentric video, which jointly reconstructs world-space hand and templated object motion, including out-of-view frames. HOT3D-CLIP ADD/ADD-S 51.1/69.9, against FoundationPose 36.1/51.9.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: ComPose: When to Trust Hands for Object Pose Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Hand-aware 6DoF RGB object tracking that adaptively fuses hand-joint and object cues from foundation models. On DexYCB, relative rotation error 1.5 deg and absolute rotation error 19.5 deg; on HO-3D v2, relative rotation error 2.4 deg. Admits failure when both hand and geometry cues degrade.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Towards in-the-wild Egocentric 3D Hand-Object Pose Estimation (EPIC-Contact, HOPformer)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: New in-the-wild egocentric dataset (2.3K clips) with posed meshes and contacts, plus a transformer that jointly predicts bimanual hand and object pose. 82.4 percent success on ARCTIC (+6.2 points).

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: AgentSTAR: Agentic Shape Tracking and Reconstruction from Monocular Videos
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Render-and-compare object tracking with a VLM agent for large motion, articulation and severe occlusion. Claims to beat all evaluated rigid-object trackers on HOT3D and point trackers on ARCTIC; numbers not checked.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: EgoGrasp: World-Space Hand-Object Interaction Estimation from Egocentric Videos
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Foundation-model preprocessing plus HOI-prior diffusion for hand-aware 6DoF object pose infilling under egocentric occlusion, for open-vocabulary objects.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Reconstructing Objects along Hand Interaction Timelines in Egocentric Video (ROHIT, COP)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Propagates object pose along static, grasp and release timelines with stable-grasp constraints on HOT3D and EPIC-Kitchens. Improves reconstruction by 6.2-11.3 percent; evaluation uses 2D projection error for lack of 3D ground truth.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: AGILE: Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction from Video via Agentic Generation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Generates a watertight object mesh with a VLM-guided generative model, then anchors the pose at the interaction onset and tracks it. Avoids SfM; evaluated on HO3D, DexYCB and ARCTIC.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Grasp in Gaussians: Fast Monocular Reconstruction of Dynamic Hand-Object Interactions
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Object initialized with SAM3D, then tracked with a compact Sum-of-Gaussians plus contact losses; 4.4x-38.9x faster than prior hand-object reconstruction.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: TwinTrack: Bridging Vision and Contact Physics for Real-Time Tracking of Unknown Objects in Contact-Rich Scenes
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Fuses a visual tracker with contact-dynamics predictions in an MJX simulator for real-time 6-DoF tracking during in-hand manipulation (above 20 Hz).

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: KineFuse: Kinematic-Aware Haptic Fusion for In-Hand Occluded-Object Pose Tracking
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Adds finger-level haptic tokens (proprioception, force, contact) to a pretrained visual pose tracker to handle finger occlusion on robot hands.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: MagicHOI: Leveraging 3D Priors for Accurate Hand-object Reconstruction from Short Monocular Video Clips
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Novel-view-synthesis diffusion prior that regularizes the occluded object regions during hand-object reconstruction.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: HOSt3R: Keypoint-free Hand-Object 3D Reconstruction from RGB images
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Keypoint-free estimation of hand-object transforms from monocular video, without templates or intrinsics; state of the art on SHOWMe.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Recovering Physically Plausible Human-Object Interactions from Monocular Videos (RePHO)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Body-object side: RL physics refinement of kinematic HOI estimates, which improves plausibility metrics. Does not directly target object pose error.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: BOP Challenge 2024 on Model-Based and Model-Free 6D Object Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Introduces the BOP-H3 hand-held AR/VR datasets and model-free onboarding tracks. The BOP 2025 challenge continues the H3 tracks 4-7; no 2025 H3 result was verified.

evidence.crowdedness: MEDIUM-HIGH. I counted about 15 relevant 2025-2026 papers, from strong groups: the HOT3D/BOP organizers, Ye (WHOLE), Damen (EPIC-Contact, ROHIT), SIGGRAPH and robotics labs. The space is fragmented by setting (egocentric RGB with templates, prior-free, hand-cue fusion, haptics), and no single benchmark is saturated.
evidence.trend: Attention is rising. Monthly 2026 arXiv output on hand-aware object tracking has grown (WHOLE, EgoGrasp, ComPose, GRC-Pose, AgentSTAR, Grasp in Gaussians, HOPformer at ECCV 2026). The drivers are robot learning from human video, the HOT3D/BOP-H3 benchmarks, and new foundation models (SAM3D, video diffusion) that people are adapting to the occlusion problem.

skeptics.reasons:
I found no 2025-2026 work that solves P04, and the newest work I could check confirms it. The web search budget was already used up, so the evidence below comes from WebFetch of arXiv abstract and HTML pages and the BOP site.

(1) GRC-Pose (arXiv 2609.39116, 30 Sep 2026) is the newest state of the art for prior-free monocular 6D tracking on HOT3D. Its table: GRC-Pose Avg AR 34.0, Motion 26.9; GigaPose 31.4; FoundationPose 3.4; RGBTrack 3.4. The authors name large inter-frame motion, severe hand occlusion, motion blur and intermittent visibility as causes of drift and tracking loss.

(2) AgentSTAR (arXiv 2609.24487, Sep 2026; Malik, Shafiullah et al.) is the best HOT3D rigid tracker. It still has a mean rotation error of 37.6 deg (median 26.3) and a mean translation error of 3.04 cm. The baselines are worse: SAM3D-Tracker 51.6 deg, FoundationPose+VGGT 54.6 deg, GigaPose+GoTrack 55.4 deg. It also costs about 10 hours of optimization per loop. The paper notes that orientation can change by 180 deg between keyframes and that hands severely occlude the object.

(3) The BOP HOT3D leaderboard for model-free 6D detection of unseen objects improved from 0.489 AP (gfreedet2, Sep 2025) to 0.531 AP (X0, May 2026). That is progress, but it is not saturation. For comparison, BOP-Classic-Core is near 0.845 AR, although that is a different metric. I could not load the model-based BOP-H3 per-dataset table.

(4) EgoXtreme (arXiv 2603.25135, Mar 2026) reports that generalizable pose estimators fail under extreme egocentric conditions.

(5) The fixes I found are side-steps, not solutions. ViTa-Zero (2504.13179) and KineFuse (2607.14842) add tactile or haptic sensing on robot hands, which does not apply to observing a human hand. AURORA (2609.08493) is CAD-free in-hand reconstruction, and I could not confirm any benchmark numbers for it.

(6) For whole-body HOI on BEHAVE and InterCap, I found only incremental 2025 gains: about 9 percent better object meshes in 2503.06012. I found nothing showing object error close to body error. I could not verify recent absolute BEHAVE object errors.

Caveat against the pain point as written: the strongest numbers it cites come from prior-free or monocular egocentric settings. With a known CAD model, a static RGB-D camera, slow motion and good masks (FoundationPose plus SAM2/SAM3 with re-initialization), tracking is closer to engineering, and I found no 2025-2026 benchmark that isolates that regime. So the claim should be narrowed, not dropped.

skeptics.reframe: Tracking a rigid object while hands hold and move it is not solved where it is hardest. The hard regime has fast in-hand rotation (up to 180 deg between HOT3D keyframes), heavy hand occlusion and intermittent visibility. There, the best September 2026 trackers still have about 26-38 deg rotation error or about 34 AR, and they run either far from real time (AgentSTAR, about 10 hours per optimization loop) or without CAD priors. The easy regime is a different case: known CAD model, static RGB-D camera, slow motion and good masks (FoundationPose plus SAM2/SAM3 with resets). That regime is close to engineering, and no 2025-2026 benchmark separates it out. The open research problem is real-time joint hand-object tracking that uses the tracked hands (contact, grasp, and hand-to-hand handover in bimanual tasks) to carry the object pose through occlusion and fast rotation. It should be scored with motion-aware metrics, such as HOT3D Motion or rotation error during the grasp, not with per-frame detection AP.

skeptics.reasons:
Artifact test, short version: the pain point is not an artifact of one dataset or one group. Its size, though, is inflated by old or weak baselines, and it holds only for some sensing settings.

1. Breadth (survives). I mapped the 53 supporting ids through the w3_digest corpus. They come from several independent groups and settings. These include Meta Reality Labs (HOT3D; BOP-H3 with CTU), MPI/Tuebingen (BEHAVE, RHOBIN), Tsinghua (HOI4D), SJTU (OakInk), ETH (ARCTIC), Bristol (HD-EPIC, VISOR-based work), industrial and cluttered 6D benchmarks (XYZ-IBD, IndustryShapes, GraspClutter6D) and robot-learning corpora and surveys (EgoVerse, HumanNet, CosmoH2G, Robot Learning from Human Videos survey). They span egocentric headsets, studios, kitchens, whole-body Kinect and single-hand demonstrations. So this is not one community's convention.

2. Magnitudes come from old or weak baselines (partly refuted).
(a) The "object error 2 to 5 times body error" claim cites the 2022 BEHAVE tracker: 21.20 vs 4.99 cm. In VisTracker (CVPR 2023, single monocular RGB) the BEHAVE Chamfer error is object 8.04 vs SMPL 5.25 cm. Under 10-frame alignment it is 8.49 vs 7.81 cm, close to equal. InterCap gives 10.32 vs 6.76. That is about 1.5 times, not 2 to 5. I verified these from the VisTracker paper.
(b) The "one-third recall" figure on HOT3D comes from FoundPose. That baseline is single-frame, RGB-only, without refinement and without temporal tracking. It is not a hand-held tracker. I verified 25.2/33.8 percent (Aria) and 28.9/36.9 percent (Quest3).
(c) The BOP-H3 drop (31.2 vs 50.4 AP) is real. But BOP-H3 also contains HOPEv2, which has no hands, and the BOP 2024 report itself says participation in the H3 tracks was limited by time and effort. So the gap partly reflects immature submissions. By 2026 the BOP model-free 6D detection leaderboard on HOT3D shows 0.531 AP (2026-05) and 0.489 (gfreedet2, 2025-09). That is already at the 2024 Classic-Core model-based level.
(d) The HOI4D figure (86.5 to 19.3) is a 2022 measurement on category-level trackers of that time.

3. Another community treats close-range RGB-D hand-held tracking as largely solved (partly refuted). BundleSDF (NVIDIA, CVPR 2023) reports on HO3D, which is RGB-D, third-person, one hand with YCB objects:
- ADD-S AUC 96.52, ADD AUC 92.62, CD 0.57 cm;
- BundleTrack: ADD-S 92.39, ADD 66.01.
The authors explicitly cite severe hand occlusion. The robotics 6D tracking line (FoundationPose, BundleTrack on YCBInEOAT) treats rigid in-hand tracking with RGB-D and a mesh or a first-frame mask as a working tool. Caveat: these AUC metrics are lenient (area up to 10 cm), and the masks come from propagating a first-frame mask.

4. What survives. The condition stays hard and under-measured when:
- input is egocentric or monocular RGB, often fisheye;
- objects are small, unseen or loosely modelled;
- the hand covers most of the visible surface;
- there is no per-sequence reference mask or template;
- the object moves fast or leaves the view.
The supporting papers give some evidence for the workaround claim: robot-learning pipelines replace object tracking with rigid-grasp priors or occlusion-free keyframes (CosmoH2G). Active-object segmentation (VISOR AP about 24-28 vs hand about 92; HOT3D in-hand mIoU about 55) remains a real bottleneck.

Verdict. Not refuted as an artifact of narrow sources. But the statement's quantitative framing and its claim that the problem holds across all settings are overstated. Third-person close-range RGB-D, which is closest to this author's own setup, is the regime where the problem is mostly solved. Bimanual cases may be harder, but I found no verified number for them.

Limits of this check. I could not run web searches: the session's WebSearch quota was used up, so everything above comes from WebFetch. I did not verify BOP 2025 Classic-Core numbers, the HOT3D model-based leaderboard or FoundationPose's YCBInEOAT numbers.

skeptics.reframe: Hand-held rigid-object pose tracking is largely solved with close-range third-person RGB-D plus a mesh or first-frame mask: BundleSDF reaches 96.5 ADD-S AUC on HO3D, and on BEHAVE the object error is only about 1.5 times the body error since 2023. It stays unsolved and largely unmeasured from egocentric or monocular RGB, for small or unseen objects whose visible surface the hand mostly covers, and without a per-sequence reference mask or template. Two failures dominate there: segmenting the object in the hand (about 55 mIoU on HOT3D) and re-acquiring it after it disappears behind the hand or leaves the view. Downstream robot-learning pipelines still work around this with rigid-grasp proxies or occlusion-free keyframes.

skeptics.reasons:
Not refuted, but the survival is partial. Searches were blocked because the shared WebSearch budget was used up (200 of 200). I checked the key sources with WebFetch of their arXiv abstract pages instead.

Where the refutation lands:
(1) Part of P04 is a data and benchmark problem, not a method problem. 'Most object pose datasets contain no hands', 'ground truth for moving hand-held objects is hard to obtain' and 'onboarding GT only for the first frame' are all calls for more capture and annotation money.
(2) Some of the gap closes with known engineering. Dense multi-view rigs, markers and IMUs on objects, and manual SAM2 correction already work in studios. Multi-view gives about 8 points on HOT3D, and the HOT3D CVPR 2025 abstract says multi-view methods significantly outperform single-view ones. So 'add views or sensors' is a known fix that only needs resources, and it is ruled out only by the monocular, egocentric or sparse RGB-D setting.
(3) 'Joint hand-object estimation' is not new. HOLD reconstructs hand and object together from monocular video with interaction constraints. BundleSDF tracks unknown objects through occlusion, including on HO3D. A proposal framed as 'do joint hand-object tracking' would be rejected as incremental.

Why it still survives:
The benchmark numbers show a large, measured, unexplained gap.
- HOT3D: FoundPose reaches 25 to 34 percent recall at 5 cm, 5 deg, even with ground-truth masks.
- BOP-H3: 31.2 AP versus 50.4 on BOP-Classic-Core.
- NOCS 86.5 versus HOI4D 19.3 for category-level tracking.
- BEHAVE: object error 21.2 cm versus 4.99 cm body error.
More data alone does not obviously close this gap: the occluder covers exactly the evidence the tracker needs, and in this setting no extra views are available. The BOP 2024 report states that model-free onboarding from dynamic hand-manipulation video is largely unaddressed. Since hands are tracked well (about 92 AP) and objects are not, a principled scientific question is open: can the reliably observed hand and its contacts act as the observation model for the occluded object?

Research questions a top-venue reviewer would find significant:
(a) How should a tracker fuse hand articulation and contact as a measurement of object pose, with calibrated uncertainty when visual evidence is fully occluded? This must handle symmetry ambiguity and in-grasp slip rather than a rigid-grasp prior. CosmoH2G shows slip and 19 deg orientation errors on a real robot.
(b) Can objects be onboarded model-free from the manipulation video itself, where the hand is both the occluder and the source of the motion? This is the BOP-H3 open task.
(c) Can a single shared tracker hand a pose estimate across two hands during bimanual regrasp or handover, given that each hand hides a different part of the object?
(d) How can tracking under occlusion be evaluated without per-frame ground truth? For example, self-consistency or physics-based metrics, so that the evaluation gap itself is studied rather than closed with money.

Risk: the area is crowded (FoundationPose, BundleSDF, HOLD, HOT3D/BOP-H3 challenge entrants). A contribution must target the full-occlusion and regrasp regime and show gains on HOT3D or BOP-H3 hand-held splits, not on HO3D or DexYCB alone. The score is held below 8 because half the pain point as stated is a data and annotation wish.

evidence.title: BundleSDF: Neural 6-DoF Tracking and 3D Reconstruction of Unknown Objects

skeptics.reframe: Hands are now tracked reliably (about 92 AP), but the rigid objects they hold are not (25 to 34 percent recall on HOT3D, even with ground-truth masks). The open question is how to use the observed hand articulation and contacts as the observation model for the occluded object, with calibrated uncertainty through full occlusion, symmetry, in-grasp slip and bimanual regrasp. The setting is model-free, egocentric or single RGB-D, and the work should be judged on hand-held splits (HOT3D, BOP-H3) rather than on static hand-free benchmarks.

research_questions.question: During a bimanual handover or regrasp, each hand hides a different face of the object. Can a real-time tracker treat the grasp state (no hand, left, right, both, slipping) as a discrete latent variable and use the tracked hands' articulation as a pose measurement, so that it carries the object's 6D pose through the handover window better than visual-only trackers (FoundationPose, BundleSDF) and single-hand fusion (ComPose)?
research_questions.why_top_venue: The newest hand-aware tracker, ComPose (arXiv 2605.23523, May 2026; verified from its HTML), states that it excludes bimanual handover and articulated sequences, provides no explicit uncertainty, and still drifts on long sequences. On HOT3D, GRC-Pose (34.0 AR) and AgentSTAR (rotation error 37.6 deg mean) name hand occlusion and intermittent visibility as the causes of failure. Neither uses a grasp-state model. HO-Cap (arXiv 2406.06843, verified) gives per-frame 6D object and MANO ground truth from 8 RealSense D455s plus an Azure Kinect, and 21 of its 64 sequences contain hand-to-hand transfers. So the handover regime can be measured without new capture, yet no published tracker reports results on it. A principled switching-filter formulation, with clear gains concentrated in the handover window, is a contribution reviewers can name. Without such a formulation, the work reads as a filter engineering note.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) Front end: a model-based visual tracker (FoundationPose in tracking mode, or a SAM3D or BundleSDF mesh onboarded from the first clear frames) gives a per-frame pose and a render-and-compare score. A hand estimator (WiLoR or HaMeR on RGB, refined against depth) gives both MANO hands. (2) While the object is visible and a hand is in contact (by fingertip-to-surface distance), the method estimates the grasp-relative transform T_hand_to_object online, with a running covariance. (3) Back end: a switching (interacting-multiple-model) filter on SE(3), or a Rao-Blackwellized particle filter in the style of PoseRBPF so that symmetric objects stay multi-modal. The discrete modes are free, held-left, held-right, held-both and slip. Each held mode uses hand-attached motion as the process model. The visual likelihood is occlusion-aware: pixels covered by the hand masks are down-weighted, not counted as misfits. In the both-hands mode, the two grasp constraints are fused, and the transform is handed from the giving hand to the receiving hand when contact on the giver ends. (4) Re-anchoring: once visibility returns, a global re-detection is gated by the filter posterior to avoid flips. (5) Real-time budget: 30 fps causal on one GPU. Only a small learned component (a grasp-state classifier on hand-object geometry features) is trained.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Go/no-go, about 6 weeks. Run FoundationPose tracking with SAM2 masks on a single third-person RealSense view of the 21 HO-Cap handover sequences. Use no ground-truth re-initialization after frame 0. Split each sequence into phases using ground-truth contact: approach, single-hand hold, handover window (both hands within 1 cm of the object, plus or minus 0.5 s) and post-handover. Report ADD-S AUC, the rotation error distribution and time-to-recover per phase. Kill criterion: if handover-window recall is within about 10 points of single-hand hold recall, or failures are under 5 percent of frames, drop this RQ, because third-person RGB-D is then solved for handovers too. The HO-Cap paper itself reports FoundationPose at 89.3 ADD and 95.7 ADD-S overall, which makes this outcome a real possibility. Full study if the gap holds: compare FoundationPose, BundleSDF, a rigid-grasp-prior baseline, ComPose (if code is available) and the proposed filter. Evaluate on HO-Cap handover and non-handover sequences, H2O third-person RGB-D two-hand sequences, DexYCB as a single-hand sanity check, and HOT3D clips with two-hand contact (RGB with monocular depth, as the stress test). Run ablations on the mode set, the occlusion-aware likelihood and the hand-estimator noise, plus a 30 fps timing table.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data only: HO-Cap (handover subset plus a matched non-handover subset), H2O (ICCV 2021, multi-view RGB-D with two hands and 6D object poses), DexYCB, and HOT3D clips (no depth; ground truth from OptiTrack). ARCTIC is optional because its objects are articulated. One workstation with a single 24 GB GPU is enough for FoundationPose and HaMeR inference and for training a small classifier. A consumer RGB-D camera is needed only for a qualitative live demo. No motion capture is needed; a robot arm only for an optional robot-replay demo.
research_questions.risks: (a) The gap may be small: HO-Cap reports 89.3 ADD for FoundationPose, and BundleSDF reaches 96.5 ADD-S AUC on HO3D. Close-range third-person RGB-D may already handle handovers, which is why the go/no-go comes first. (b) Only 21 handover sequences: a top vision venue may find this thin, so a second source (H2O, HOT3D two-hand clips) is needed. (c) Hand-estimator errors grow exactly when the object hides the fingers, so the hand measurement can be worse than the visual one. (d) Scooping: ComPose, HOPformer (ECCV 2026, bimanual on ARCTIC) or the WHOLE and EgoGrasp groups could add handover handling within months. (e) If the gains appear only on RGB-D third-person data, CVPR reviewers will call the regime easy, and the paper goes to ICRA or RA-L.

research_questions.question: Can a hand-held object tracker report a pose uncertainty whose coverage stays calibrated as the object goes from visible to mostly or fully hidden by the hands? Can each frame be labelled measured, inferred-from-grasp or unknown, so that robot-learning and digital-twin pipelines can filter demonstrations by how trustworthy the object pose is, instead of discarding occluded clips or assuming a rigid grasp?
research_questions.why_top_venue: None of the 2025-2026 trackers in the evidence (ComPose, GRC-Pose, WHOLE, AgentSTAR, HOPformer) reports calibrated uncertainty. ComPose's HTML states it has none. An arXiv keyword search for hand-object 6D tracking with uncertainty returned only AURORA, which is robot-side active in-hand reconstruction, and Bayes3D, which is not hand-specific. The pain point record shows human-to-robot pipelines work around the problem with rigid-grasp priors, occlusion-free keyframes or discarded clips, which is exactly the decision a calibrated per-frame trust signal would replace. Coverage under occlusion-driven distribution shift is a measurable property, and it supports a downstream claim (better policies from filtered demonstrations), which top venues reward.
research_questions.method_sketch: Wrap any base tracker, including the RQ1 filter, FoundationPose or ComPose. (1) Features per frame: visible-surface fraction, render-and-compare score, hand-object contact state, time since last confident visual fix, and agreement between hand-propagated and visual pose. (2) A small head predicts a rotation and translation error scale. (3) Adaptive conformal calibration over time, using an online adaptive conformal update because exchangeability fails in video. It is conditioned on the occlusion bin and turns the predicted scale into pose sets with target coverage, for example 90 percent. Symmetric objects use symmetry-aware set membership. (4) A three-state provenance label (measured, inferred, unknown) comes from thresholds on the calibrated set size. (5) Downstream test: retarget DexYCB or HO-Cap object trajectories into a simulator (for example, replay grasps with an Allegro or Shadow hand in Isaac or MuJoCo). Compare policy or replay success when training on all frames, on visibility-filtered frames, and on uncertainty-filtered frames.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Calibrate on DexYCB and HO-Cap training splits and test on HO-Cap handover sequences and HOT3D two-hand clips (a shifted domain). Report empirical coverage against nominal coverage per occlusion bin (0-25, 25-50, 50-75 and 75-100 percent hidden), set size, and risk-coverage curves. The main baseline is the base tracker's raw score with a threshold. Expected headline: the raw score is overconfident in the 75-100 percent bin, and the calibrated sets restore near-nominal coverage at an acceptable set size. Add one downstream simulation result showing that uncertainty filtering raises replay success over visibility filtering at equal data volume. The kill criterion is the same as RQ1: if base-tracker errors are already small in heavy-occlusion bins, the uncertainty story has nothing to calibrate.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: DexYCB, HO-Cap, HOT3D and H2O, all with per-frame ground truth. A single GPU is enough, and calibration is cheap. A simulator (MuJoCo or Isaac Gym) handles the downstream test, so no robot is needed. A real robot replay on a borrowed arm is a bonus, not a requirement.
research_questions.risks: (a) Uncertainty papers are often judged incremental unless the downstream gain is clear; the simulation replay must show a real difference. (b) Conformal guarantees in time series need adaptive or online variants, and reviewers will probe the assumptions. Prior conformal 6D pose work exists from memory (Yang and Pavone, CVPR 2023, conformal keypoints; not verified in this session) and must be cited and differentiated: the novelty here is occlusion and grasp conditioning and temporal adaptation. (c) If the base tracker fails catastrophically (180 deg flips), calibrated sets become uselessly large; multi-modal sets are needed. (d) The field may treat this as an add-on to RQ1, so it may be stronger as one section of the RQ1 paper than as a standalone paper.
target_venues: NeurIPS (only if the temporal conformal method is a contribution in itself)

research_questions.question: Where in an interaction does hand-held object tracking actually fail: grasp onset, in-hand rotation, regrasp, handover, release or out-of-view? Do current per-frame metrics (BOP AP, recall at 5 cm, 5 deg, ADD AUC) hide these failures? And can ground-truth-free proxy metrics (hand-contact consistency, penetration, reprojection and temporal consistency) be validated against ground truth, so trackers can be scored on in-the-wild video that has none?
research_questions.why_top_venue: The skeptics agree that the hard regime is under-measured. The pain point says methods are neither trained nor scored on the condition, and the artifact skeptic shows the headline gap depends heavily on setting (BundleSDF 96.5 ADD-S on HO3D against 25-34 percent recall on HOT3D). No 2025-2026 benchmark separates the easy regime from the hard one. An event-stratified, multi-dataset harness with validated GT-free metrics answers a question the community is asking (BOP-H3, EPIC-Contact, ROHIT all fall back to 2D projection error), needs no new capture, and fits a small lab's budget.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) Harmonize HOT3D, HO-Cap, DexYCB, HO3D, H2O and ARCTIC (rigid base part) into one format. (2) Derive event labels automatically from ground-truth hand-object distances and object velocity: approach, contact onset, stable hold, in-hand rotation (angular speed above a threshold), regrasp, handover, release and out-of-view. Also add per-frame visible fraction rendered from ground truth. (3) Run 6-8 public trackers in matched settings: FoundationPose, BundleSDF, GigaPose with a refiner, a SAM3D-mesh tracker, plus ComPose, GRC-Pose and HOPformer if code is released. Use single-view and causal settings, with no ground-truth re-initialization. (4) Report event-stratified accuracy, time-to-failure and time-to-recover, and HOT3D-style motion retention. (5) Propose 3-4 GT-free proxy metrics. Measure their rank correlation with ground-truth error across trackers and events, then apply the validated proxies to EPIC-Kitchens or HD-EPIC clips.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Three datasets (HO-Cap, DexYCB, HOT3D subset), three trackers (FoundationPose, BundleSDF, one RGB-only tracker), event stratification, plus one proxy metric (contact-consistency) with its correlation to ground-truth error. This could double as the RQ1 go/no-go and could be done in about 2 months. It is publishable if it shows that failures concentrate in specific events and that ranking trackers by overall AUC differs from ranking them by event-level accuracy.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public datasets only; the HOT3D and HO-Cap downloads are large but under typical lab storage. One GPU for inference across trackers (a few GPU-weeks in total). No camera, robot or motion capture needed.
research_questions.risks: (a) A benchmark built only from existing data is judged less novel; it needs a sharp, surprising finding (for example, a reversed tracker ranking, or most error coming from a few percent of frames). (b) BOP organizers or HOT3D authors may publish similar breakdowns. (c) Proxy metrics may correlate weakly with ground truth, which is still a finding, but a weaker paper. (d) Getting baselines to run consistently across six datasets costs real engineering time. (e) Venue fit is mainly the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks track, which is a good fit but competitive.

fit.thesis_assets_help: The assets give a small head start, mostly in concepts and engineering rather than data. (1) The measured/held/constrained honesty labels are a discrete form of the provenance labels in RQ2. The held state, where the object and hand are rigidly coupled, matches the held modes in RQ1. This is the most useful asset. (2) The object-conditioned recovery of the occluded holding arm is the dual of what RQ1 needs (hand to object, rather than object to arm). The coupling logic and contact gating can be reused, but the direction is inverted, so the code does not transfer directly. (3) The causal 30 fps chain and the single RGB-D desk setup match the real-time third-person RGB-D regime and give a ready live demo. That regime, though, is the one closest to solved (HO-Cap FoundationPose 89.3 ADD; BundleSDF 96.5 ADD-S on HO3D), so it is not where a top-venue claim can rest. (4) The ArUco-marked object gives metric ground truth only when the marker is visible, so it cannot score the occluded frames that matter. It can measure re-acquisition after occlusion and support a qualitative figure. (5) The Unity twin is a downstream demonstration for the digital-twin use case, not evidence. (6) The 28 recordings of one subject cannot serve as a benchmark at a top venue and are useful at most for qualitative results. Net effect: a few months saved on infrastructure and framing; no advantage in data or evaluation.
fit.what_a_small_lab_cannot_do_here: A small lab cannot capture new hand-held object ground truth at benchmark quality: HOT3D uses OptiTrack markers on objects, and HO-Cap uses 8 RealSense cameras plus a Kinect with semi-automatic annotation. A single RGB-D camera with ArUco markers cannot provide ground truth for occluded frames. It cannot compete on the prior-free egocentric HOT3D leaderboard against foundation-scale pipelines: GRC-Pose with SAM3D, WHOLE and EgoGrasp with generative hand-object motion priors, and AgentSTAR, which spends about 10 hours of optimization per loop. Nor can it train video-diffusion or large egocentric hand-object priors, or collect an in-the-wild dataset the size of EPIC-Contact (2.3K clips with posed meshes). Tactile and haptic fusion on robot hands (KineFuse, ViTa-Zero, TwinTrack's contact physics on a real hand) needs instrumented robot hands the lab does not have. Real-robot validation of downstream policies needs a borrowed arm. A credible top-venue project therefore stays on public datasets with per-frame ground truth (HO-Cap, H2O, DexYCB, HOT3D). It must target a niche the strong groups have explicitly left open: bimanual handover and regrasp, calibrated per-frame trust, and event-stratified evaluation. It must also pass the 6-week go/no-go first, because third-person RGB-D may already handle handovers well. Unverified items: whether ComPose, GRC-Pose and HOPformer have released code; per-phase FoundationPose accuracy on HO-Cap handovers; whether HOH provides per-frame 6D object poses; and the conformal 6D pose prior work (Yang and Pavone, CVPR 2023) and PoseRBPF, both cited from memory. WebSearch was exhausted, so the checks used WebFetch of arXiv abstract, HTML and search pages.

painpoint.name: Synthetic data cannot replace real interaction data

evidence.latest_state: For single-hand 3D pose, the gap has nearly closed in controlled settings. The CVPR 2025 synthetic-to-real gap study (arXiv 2503.19307) reports synthetic-only training reaching 84-97 percent of real-only accuracy on FreiHAND (for example simpleHand 0.77 vs 0.65 cm PA-MPJPE, S2HAND 1.02 vs 0.99 cm) and about 0.86-0.87 cm on DexYCB. It names the forearm, image frequency statistics, pose distribution and object occlusion as the missing ingredients, and it notes that stronger models overfit synthetic data more and that the gap is larger on heavily occluded hand-object frames. At scale, AnyHand (arXiv 2603.25726, 2026; 2.5M single-hand plus 4.1M hand-object RGB-D images) gives only small gains when added to real data: HO-3D v2 PA-MPJPE 7.7 to 7.47 mm for HaMeR and 7.5 to 7.36 mm for WiLoR, FreiHAND 6.0 to 5.55 mm. Its authors report that 100 percent synthetic training underperforms mixed training, that a 50-75 percent synthetic share is best, and that compositing artifacts remain (background depth noise, mismatched intrinsics). For egocentric HOI detection, HOI-Synth (arXiv 2603.29733) still frames synthetic data as a complement: synthetic data plus 10 percent of the real labels gains +5.67 AP on VISOR, +8.24 on EgoHOS and +11.69 on ENIGMA-51 over real-only, and the gains grow with how closely the synthetic objects, grasps and environments match each benchmark. Generative sim-to-real video is the newest route: PAM (CVPR 2026) shows SimpleHand trained on 50 percent of the real DexYCB data plus 207k generated frames matches the 100 percent real baseline. For bodies, BEDLAM2.0 (NeurIPS 2025 D&B oral) improves world-coordinate human motion but adds cameras, shoes, clothing and environments, not object interaction, so the missing-contact problem for synthetic humans remains. For object pose, the BOP Challenge 2024 report moves to real-world BOP-H3 headset data and reports unseen-object 2D detection still 35 percent behind seen objects. A 2026 industrial sim-to-real review (arXiv 2605.30581) concludes that render count alone does not close the T-LESS/BOP transfer gap and that small real calibration sets matter more. No paper found reports synthetic-only training matching real data for bimanual or hand-object RGB-D tracking with contact.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Analyzing the Synthetic-to-Real Domain Gap in 3D Hand Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: First systematic study of the synthetic-to-real gap for 3D hand pose; identifies forearm, frequency statistics, pose and object occlusion as the key factors; synthetic-only reaches 84-97 percent of real on FreiHAND, and the gap is larger under object occlusion.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: AnyHand: A Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for RGB(-D) Hand Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Releases 2.5M single-hand and 4.1M hand-object synthetic RGB-D images with arm, occlusion and depth; gives small gains on HO-3D and FreiHAND when mixed with real data; synthetic-only training underperforms mixed training.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Leveraging Synthetic Data for Enhancing Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Detection (HOI-Synth)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Pipeline and HOI-Synth benchmark on VISOR, EgoHOS and ENIGMA-51; synthetic plus 10 percent of the real labels beats real-only (+5.67, +8.24, +11.69 AP); shows gains grow with closer synthetic-real alignment of objects, grasps and environments.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: PAM: A Pose-Appearance-Motion Engine for Sim-to-Real HOI Video Generation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Diffusion-based hand-object video generation from simulated pose; 207k generated frames plus 50 percent of real DexYCB match the 100 percent real hand-pose baseline (DexYCB MPJPE 19.37 mm generation fidelity, OAKINK2 FVD 46.31).

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: BEDLAM2.0: Synthetic Humans and Cameras in Motion
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Larger and more realistic synthetic human video set with camera motion for world-coordinate pose; does not add object interaction or contact, which is part of P05.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: HVG-3D: Bridging Real and Simulation Domains for 3D-Conditional Hand-Object Interaction Video Synthesis
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: 3D-ControlNet video diffusion that turns simulated or real 3D hand-object control signals into realistic HOI video (TASTE-Rob) to make simulated data usable.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: EgoInteract: Synthetic Egocentric Videos Generation for Interaction Understanding and Anticipation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Controllable egocentric simulator with body, hand and object manipulation; reports consistent gains on real egocentric benchmarks including HOI detection when synthetic data is added.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Learning Generalizable Hand-Object Tracking from Synthetic Demonstrations
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Learns physics-based dexterous hand-object tracking controllers purely from synthesized trajectories (HOP planner and HOT tracker), with no human demonstrations; a control result, not visual perception.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Policy-as-Data: Learning Generalizable HOI Diffusion Models from Simulated Physics
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Generates whole-body human-object interaction data from RL policies in a physics simulator and retargets it to parametric bodies, addressing the lack of interaction in synthetic humans for motion generation.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: BOP Challenge 2024 on Model-Based and Model-Free 6D Object Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Moves BOP toward real-world BOP-H3 headset data and model-free onboarding; reports unseen-object 2D detection still 35 percent behind seen objects, the main bottleneck.

evidence.crowdedness: MEDIUM-HIGH: at least 10 papers from 2025-2026 attack it from four directions (hand datasets such as AnyHand and the CVPR 2025 gap study, egocentric HOI-Synth and EgoInteract, generative sim-to-real video such as PAM at CVPR 2026 and HVG-3D, and BEDLAM2.0 and BOP for bodies and objects). Strong groups are involved (MPI Tuebingen, UCSD, the BOP organisers, Catania FPV-IPLab). Contact-accurate bimanual and RGB-D interaction synthesis with realistic sensor noise is still thinly covered.
evidence.trend: rising: generative video models (diffusion sim-to-real engines) and physics-simulated interaction generation in 2026 have turned synthetic HOI data from rendering-only into a fast-growing line, driven by embodied-AI and robot-data demand. Contact realism and sensor-noise fidelity are still the stated limits.

skeptics.reasons:
I found no 2025-2026 work that solves P05 for hand-object or body-object interaction. Some sub-claims have shrunk, though, so the statement as written is too broad. Note: the shared WebSearch budget was used up (200 of 200 calls), so every check below was a WebFetch of arXiv abstract, HTML or search pages, and coverage is narrower than planned.

(1) Object pose on standard rigid-object benchmarks is close to closed, and this part of P05 is overstated. The BOP Challenge 2024 report (arXiv 2504.02812) says the best unseen-object method, FreeZeV2.1, reaches 82.1 AR on BOP-Classic-Core. That is 3.5 points behind the best seen-object method (GPose2023, 85.6 AR). I read this as near-parity for synthetic-only training, because unseen-object methods are trained on synthetic data (inferred; the report does not state it in these terms). The same report shows the gap returns for hand-held objects: on the new BOP-H3 datasets (HOT3D, HOPEv2, HANDAL), GigaPose+GenFlow scores 31.2 AP for 6D detection versus 50.4 AP on BOP-Classic-Core. So the gap that remains is tied to interaction (hand occlusion, egocentric headset sensors), not to synthetic rendering in general.

(2) Hands: the newest large synthetic sets still only add to real data. AnyHand (arXiv 2603.25726, March 2026) has 2.5M single-hand and 4.1M hand-object RGB-D images. It reports gains on FreiHAND and HO-3D only when added to the existing real-data training recipes. The abstract reports no synthetic-only result and makes no claim that synthetic data replaces real data.

(3) Generated hand-object video cuts the need for real data but does not remove it. PAM (arXiv 2603.22193, March 2026) shows that 3,400 generated videos (207k frames) plus 50 percent of the real data match the 100 percent real baseline on DexYCB/OAKINK2. That halves the real data needed; it does not replace it, and no synthetic-only result is given.

(4) Bodies: BEDLAM2.0 (arXiv 2511.14394, Nov 2025) improves on BEDLAM for world-coordinate body estimation. Its abstract makes no claim about adding object interaction or about synthetic-only parity with real data. The interaction-free limitation in P05 (paper 1239) is untouched by it.

Overall, the gap has been closed for rigid objects without hands and narrowed for bodies without objects. It stays open where hands, contact, grasp approach and real depth-sensor noise matter, which is the core of the author's field. The pain point survives, but should be narrowed to that interaction-specific gap.

skeptics.reframe: Synthetic data now nearly matches real data for rigid objects with no hands (BOP-Classic-Core, 82.1 vs 85.6 AR) and helps for bodies with no objects (BEDLAM2.0). It still cannot replace real data once a hand is in contact with the object: hand-held object pose falls to 31.2 AP on BOP-H3 versus 50.4 AP on BOP-Classic-Core (BOP 2024 report). The newest synthetic hand-object image and video generators (AnyHand, PAM) only add to real data or halve the amount needed, and report no synthetic-only result. The open problem is simulating contact, the grasp approach, hand occlusion of the object and real RGB-D sensor noise accurately enough that interaction data can be generated rather than captured.

skeptics.reasons:
Artifact test: the support is not narrow. P05 rests on about 50 distinct works from at least three separate communities: egocentric HOI and hand pose, body HPS and egocentric body, and rigid 6D object pose. These come from unrelated groups and venues (Catania/ECCV 2024 VISOR study, RenderIH ICCV 2023, BEDLAM/BEDLAM2.0, UnrealEgo/EgoSim, XYZ-IBD ECCV 2026, IndustryShapes ICRA 2026, PACE, ClearPose, HANDAL, AnyHand 2026, Thalhammer T-RO 2024 challenges paper). No single dataset or lab drives it.

The broad statement still fails in two of its three subfields, where other communities treat synthetic-only training as largely solved.
(1) Body HPS. BEDLAM (CVPR 2023, abstract verified) states that networks trained only on synthetic data reach state-of-the-art accuracy on real-image HPS benchmarks. P05's body evidence is narrower than "synthetic cannot replace real": synthetic humans lack handled objects and contact, and BEDLAM2.0 says from-scratch backbones trail COCO-pretrained ones.
(2) Rigid object pose. The BOP 2020 report (verified) found that a method trained on PBR-only RGB ranked fifth of 26 and that PBR photorealism was effective. FoundationPose (CVPR 2024, verified) trains on large-scale synthetic data and beats specialised methods on real benchmarks. The BOP 2023 report (verified) says the best unseen-object method, trained without real images of the target, matched the best 2020 seen-object method.
The big collapses P05 cites (GDRN 0.827 to 0.266, recall 76.4 to 8.9) come from new real-data benchmark papers built around deliberately hard industrial, cluttered or transparent conditions. Their genre has an incentive to show sim-to-real failure, so these drops are partly a selection-and-framing artifact, not a field-wide failure. P05 itself admits that gains on standard benchmarks may reflect dataset-specific domain randomisation.

What survives across independent groups is the interaction-specific gap. Synthetic-only hand and HOI training trails real by large margins:
- VISOR mask AP 9.88 vs 45.33 (Leonardi ECCV 2024);
- RenderIH-only 13.50 vs 6.76 mm (ICCV 2023);
- AnyHand gains saturate beyond 2-4M samples.
Synthetic humans omit object contact and grasp approach, and simulated depth lacks real sensor artefacts. The pain point is therefore real but overstated. As written it bundles a solved-enough body/rigid-object sim-to-real story with a still-open hand-contact rendering problem.

Not verified in this pass: the hand-side numbers were not re-fetched. The WebSearch budget was exhausted, so I could not check for a recent synthetic-only hand model that matches real data on FreiHAND or HO3D.

skeptics.reframe: Synthetic data now matches real data for body-only pose and for rigid-object pose on standard benchmarks (BEDLAM, BOP PBR, FoundationPose). It still cannot replace real data for hand-object interaction. Renderers cannot produce realistic grasp approach, finger-object contact and deformation, hand-occluded object appearance, or real RGB-D sensor artefacts. As a result, hand and HOI models trained only on synthetic data trail real-data training by large margins, and the gains stop growing as more synthetic data is added. The open problem is interaction-faithful and sensor-faithful synthesis, not sim-to-real in general.

skeptics.reasons:
The refutation holds for P05 as worded, but not for the problem behind it. Worded as "synthetic data cannot replace real data", it describes the state of the field and asks no question. Read that way it is engineering and data work: better renders, more assets, more mocap. The usual fix in the evidence, mixing real and synthetic data (RenderIH mixed 5.79 mm vs 6.76 mm real-only), is already known and needs nothing but resources. A paper that says "we rendered more" goes to a datasets-and-benchmarks track, not a main CVPR/ICCV/NeurIPS track.

Three things save it from full refutation.
(1) The gap has a known boundary, and that makes it a research question. BEDLAM (CVPR 2023) shows that synthetic-only training reaches state-of-the-art body pose and shape on real images. The P05 evidence shows synthetic-only training failing for hands with objects, egocentric HOI masks (9.88 vs 45.33 AP) and PBR object pose on new real setups (0.827 to 0.266 AP). So the open question is: what is it about interaction that rendering does not capture, and can each part be modelled? Candidate parts are contact geometry, the grasp approach and the arm, hand-object occlusion, and depth-sensor artifacts. A controlled study that adds these factors one at a time and measures how much of the gap each closes would be a main-track paper. Nobody in the evidence has done it; papers list the causes without measuring them.
(2) There is a method question with recent top-venue precedent. Generative interaction synthesis with 3D labels that stay consistent with the image is the direction of HandBooster and HOIDiffusion (both arXiv 2024; reported as CVPR 2024, venue not verified here) and of Re:InterHand relighting (NeurIPS 2023 D&B). These works show gains from mixed training only. A "BEDLAM for hand-object interaction" that matches real-only training with synthetic data alone would be significant, as would a learned RGB-D sensor-noise model for close-range hands.
(3) Evaluation question. BOP 2020 reports that PBR training is effective on the standard benchmarks, yet XYZ-IBD reports a collapse on new real bins. So reported sim-to-real gains may partly reflect domain randomisation tuned to each dataset. That is a methodological claim a reviewer would care about.

Weaknesses that keep the score moderate:
- The most valuable outcome, synthetic-only parity, needs large asset, mocap and compute budgets; small labs are poorly placed.
- The diagnostic study risks being judged an analysis or D&B paper.
- Diffusion-based synthesis is crowded.
- The pain point bundles three subfields (hands, bodies, object pose) that have different causes.

Web search budget was exhausted, so verification used arXiv abstract pages; CVF and dblp pages returned 403 or access-denied.
