skeptics.reframe: Human demonstrations cannot be turned into robot-view observations that are physically faithful. Converted images and videos keep the wrong contact region and mode, a wrong object trajectory, and wrong robot-scene occlusion, because conversion relies on 2D masks or generative priors instead of reconstructed 4D hand-object geometry and contact. No existing metric of converted data predicts whether it will help a policy: video quality ranks weakly against transfer validity. The open question is how much 3D hand-object reconstruction and contact accuracy bounds human-to-robot transfer, and whether geometry-grounded conversion plus a contact-aware validity metric closes the gap.

research_questions.question: RQ1 (strongest). How much 3D hand-object reconstruction error can human-to-robot transfer tolerate, and which error component sets the limit? The candidate components are metric wrist depth and translation, hand-object relative pose, object 6D pose, the contact set, temporal jitter and occlusion dropouts. A second question is whether the standard HOI metrics (MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, object ADD) predict executability at all.
research_questions.why_top_venue: The field names 3D hand-object pose and contact as the bottleneck of human-to-robot transfer. The P35 record states this in why_it_persists, and all three skeptics converge on the same point. Yet no paper found quantifies the relationship. I read four abstracts. C2Dex (arXiv 2608.07045, Aug 2026, submitted to RA-L, single hand, DexYCB and TACO, end-to-end trajectory success 57.78 and 26.67 percent) and RoboWheel (arXiv 2512.02729, Dec 2025) both improve reconstruction for transfer, but their abstracts do not relate error components to downstream success. ManipTrans (CVPR 2025, arXiv 2503.21860) and DexMachina (arXiv 2505.24853) transfer motion-capture HOI data to robot hands in simulation, so they show what clean input achieves and leave open what estimated input does. Three arXiv listing searches for sensitivity or executability studies returned nothing; that is not exhaustive, and WebSearch was unavailable. An error budget would tell the HOI-reconstruction community which quantity to optimize, which is a field-level insight rather than another pipeline. That framing can carry a CoRL or NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks paper, and a CVPR or ICCV paper if it comes with a budget-guided estimator improvement.
research_questions.method_sketch: (1) Ground-truth replay. Take motion-capture or multi-view-annotated HOI sequences and retarget them to two embodiments in a physics simulator: a parallel-jaw gripper through a grasp-frame mapping, and one dexterous hand through kinematic plus contact-optimization retargeting with an optional short residual-RL refinement, following the ManipTrans and DexMachina designs. Record replay success, defined as the object reaching the GT trajectory within tolerance without a drop, together with contact preservation. (2) Structured perturbation. Inject error along each axis separately and jointly. Use noise models fitted to residuals of real estimators, not isotropic Gaussian noise: per-sequence depth bias and scale error, hand-object relative offset, object rotation error, contact dropout and shift, temporal jitter, and frame dropouts in occluded segments. Sweep levels to get tolerance curves per axis and per embodiment. Decompose sensitivity with variance-based indices or a regression of success on the per-axis errors. (3) Real estimators. Run off-the-shelf pipelines on the same sequences: monocular hand meshes (HaMeR, WiLoR) with FoundationPose objects, a monocular HOI method (for example HOLD), and the same pipelines with RGB-D depth alignment. Measure their per-axis errors and executability, and test whether the budget predicts their ranking better than MPJPE or ADD. (4) Proof of use. Apply one cheap fix that the budget points to, such as contact-consistent refinement or metric depth anchoring from RGB-D, and show that it moves executability more than it moves MPJPE.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Use two datasets: DexYCB (single hand) and ARCTIC (bimanual, articulated). Use two embodiments (gripper and one dexterous hand) and at least two retargeters, so that the conclusions are not an artifact of one retargeter. Run five error axes at six levels each on about 200 sequences, which gives tolerance curves and a sensitivity ranking. Add three to four real estimator pipelines on the same sequences, and report rank correlation (Kendall or Spearman) of executability against MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, ADD and the proposed budget-weighted error. Add one estimator modification guided by the budget, with its executability gain. No real robot is needed for the core result. Replaying 10-20 trajectories on a borrowed arm would make it far more credible at CoRL or ICRA.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data: DexYCB, HO3D v3, ARCTIC; optionally OakInk2, TACO, HOT3D or GigaHands for breadth. All have motion-capture or multi-view GT for hand and object. Simulation: IsaacGym or IsaacLab, or MuJoCo/ManiSkill, on one 24-48 GB GPU. Massively parallel environments make the perturbation sweep affordable if per-trajectory residual RL is kept short or replaced by a shared residual policy. Estimator inference runs on the same GPU. No motion capture is needed. A robot arm is optional: borrow one for a short real replay sanity check.
research_questions.risks: (1) Retargeter dependence. Residual RL can absorb error and make every axis look harmless. Mitigate with several retargeters and report absorption as a finding. (2) Simulated replay success is a proxy, and reviewers at CoRL and RSS will ask for real-robot or policy-level evidence that a small lab cannot supply at scale. (3) Scoop risk is high and time-sensitive. C2Dex, RoboWheel and ManipTrans follow-ups could add noise ablations at any time, and the area moved monthly through 2026. (4) An analysis-only paper is often judged incremental at CVPR or ICCV unless it yields a metric or method others adopt. (5) The noise models must be realistic; isotropic noise will be criticized. (6) Code release status for ManipTrans and DexMachina was not verified.

research_questions.question: RQ2. Can a geometry-grounded validity score detect when robotized human video or images fail to preserve contact, object trajectory and embodiment? The score would reconstruct the 4D robot-gripper and object state from the converted video and compare it with the 4D hand-object state reconstructed from the source human video. The test is whether it tracks transfer validity better than video-quality metrics and MLLM judges.
research_questions.why_top_venue: H2R-Bench (arXiv 2608.13049, Aug 2026; abstract read) reports that leading video world models fail on embodiment consistency and functional contact. Per the P35 record, H2RCore spans 30.0 to 84.6 while video quality spans only 0.73 to 0.81, with weak rank association. The P35 record also states that generic video-quality and VLM metrics do not detect these failures. HandEdit rejects about a third of its pseudo-pairs through human screening (from the P35 record; not independently verified). A reliable, automatic, geometry-based judge would serve every robotization pipeline (Phantom, Masquerade, HuRo, RoboEdit, Mitty) as a filter and as an evaluation metric. Contributing an evaluation in a crowded race fits a small lab well, because it does not require out-generating large labs.
research_questions.method_sketch: From the source human clip, reconstruct the metric hand-object trajectory and a per-frame contact region on the object mesh. From the converted robot clip, track the object with a model-based 6D tracker and fit the robot end effector by fitting a known gripper CAD or kinematic model to masks and depth (estimated monocular depth if no sensor depth exists). Score object-trajectory agreement, contact-region overlap on the object surface (IoU or a Chamfer distance on contact patches), contact timing and mode (grasp onset, release, pinch versus power), gripper-object penetration and floating, and actor leakage (a residual human hand detector). Calibrate the combined score against two kinds of ground truth: (a) human labels of transfer validity, from H2R-Bench if released, or a few hundred clips labelled in house; and (b) simulated replay success of the trajectory implied by the robot clip.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Take converted clips from three to five pipelines with public code or released outputs, on 150-300 source clips drawn from HOI datasets with GT (DexYCB, ARCTIC, HOT3D), so that the source-side reconstruction can also be checked against GT. Report rank correlation of the geometric score with human validity labels and with simulated replay success, and compare against video FVD or quality metrics, an MLLM judge and CLIP-style similarity. Add an ablation of each geometric term. As a utility demo, show that using the score to filter a robotization pipeline's pseudo-pairs reduces the number of human-rejected pairs.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public HOI datasets with GT, plus generated clips from open robotization or video-editing pipelines. Running open video models such as Wan 2.2-based editors at inference time on one GPU is feasible but slow; reuse released outputs where possible. Human labelling of a few hundred clips can be done by the two students. A single GPU and no robot are enough. An MLLM API budget for the judge baseline is needed (small).
research_questions.risks: (1) Release of the H2R-Bench clips and labels is unverified. Without it, all validity labels must be self-collected, which reviewers may view as biased. (2) Generated videos can be so physically inconsistent that 4D reconstruction of the robot fails. That failure is partly the signal, but it must be separated from tracker failure. (3) Metric papers need adoption, and a large lab could ship a similar judge inside its own benchmark. (4) Correlation with real policy success, the quantity that ultimately matters, cannot be shown without a robot and many policy runs.

research_questions.question: RQ3 (weaker, narrower). In bimanual handling where one hand is heavily occluded, does object-conditioned completion of the occluded hand raise bimanual transfer executability relative to frame-wise hand estimators? Object-conditioned completion means inferring the hand's pose from the tracked object pose and a contact or grasp prior. A second question is whether per-frame provenance labels (measured versus inferred) let a transfer pipeline reject segments that would fail.
research_questions.why_top_venue: Bimanual transfer is the hardest case: Masquerade targets bimanual kitchen tasks, and DexMachina targets bimanual dexterous retargeting from ARCTIC. Occlusion of one hand by the object or the other hand is a dominant error source that RQ1 is expected to expose. C2Dex is single hand only, per its abstract. Showing that occlusion-aware HOI recovery changes downstream executability would link the HOI-reconstruction and robot-learning communities. On its own this is more likely an ICRA or RA-L contribution than a CVPR one, unless the completion model is itself novel and general.
research_questions.method_sketch: Track the object in metric 6D with RGB-D, using model-based tracking. When a hand's visibility drops, infer its pose from a learned grasp-conditioned prior given the object pose, the last observed contact and temporal smoothness, and emit a per-frame provenance and confidence label. Evaluate on bimanual GT data with natural occlusion, plus synthetic occlusion masks with controlled duration. Feed the outputs into the RQ1 simulation harness to measure executability with and without completion, and with and without confidence gating.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Use ARCTIC and one more bimanual GT dataset (OakInk2, TACO or HOT3D). Bin occlusion duration into short, medium and long. Compare four conditions: frame-wise estimator, temporal smoothing baseline, object-conditioned completion, and completion plus confidence gating. Metrics: hand error on occluded frames, contact-F1 and bimanual replay success in simulation. Add a small real qualitative set from a desk RGB-D setup.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: ARCTIC, OakInk2, TACO or HOT3D; the RQ1 simulation harness; one GPU; one consumer RGB-D camera for qualitative real clips. No motion capture or robot is needed.
research_questions.risks: (1) Incremental relative to existing grasp-synthesis and HOI-prior work. Novelty rests on showing the downstream executability effect, so it depends on RQ1 being done first. (2) The gain may be small if residual RL in the retargeter already repairs short occlusions. (3) Single-lab evaluation with no robot limits the venue to ICRA or RA-L-level unless the results are striking.

fit.thesis_assets_help: Small, mostly conceptual. (1) The object-conditioned recovery of an occluded holding arm is directly the seed of RQ3. It would need to be generalized from one rig and one subject to public bimanual datasets with GT before it counts as evidence. (2) The measured, held and constrained honesty labels map naturally onto the per-frame confidence gating proposed in RQ3, and onto the source-side reliability term in RQ2. That is a genuine idea-level edge, but it is cheap to replicate. (3) The single RGB-D desk setup with ArUco metric object pose can supply a small real-world qualitative set with metric object GT. It has no hand GT (no motion capture), only one subject and 28 recordings, so it cannot be a benchmark and carries no quantitative weight at a top venue. (4) The Unity twin and the causal 30 fps chain add little: the simulation work belongs in IsaacGym, IsaacLab or MuJoCo, where the retargeting baselines live. Net: the assets help motivate and prototype RQ3 and the gating idea, and give none of the headline evidence. The main results must come from public datasets.
fit.what_a_small_lab_cannot_do_here: A small lab cannot compete in the pixel-robotization race itself. That race needs fine-tuning of video diffusion or world models at Wan 2.2 or Cosmos scale, building hundreds of thousands of robotized episodes (HuRo reports 630K, RoboEdit 174K pairs), and VLA pretraining on them. Each takes multi-GPU clusters and large-lab engineering. Without owning robots, the lab also cannot capture real pixel-aligned or paired human-robot data: mirrored VR teleoperation workspaces, UMI re-enactment and multi-embodiment rigs all need hardware. It cannot run policy-level evaluation at the scale CoRL, RSS and ICRA reviewers expect (many tasks, many trials, several embodiments) with only a borrowed arm. It cannot build large egocentric or ego-exo corpora, and it cannot produce motion-capture-grade hand GT of its own. The viewpoint and cross-view association part of P35 (the EgoExoLearn-style problem) is a separate video-understanding problem and should be dropped. What remains feasible is the reconstruction and evaluation side: error budgets, executability metrics and occlusion-aware HOI recovery, measured in simulation on public GT datasets, with at most a small real-robot sanity check.

painpoint.name: Symmetric objects make pose ambiguous and metrics inconsistent

evidence.latest_state: The problem is still open in 2025-2026. The newer methods split into three families, and none of them combines unseen objects, no symmetry labels, and a standard metric. (1) Evaluation. BOP-Distrib (Meden, Lepetit et al., WACV 2026) re-annotates T-LESS and other BOP sets with image-specific visual ambiguities instead of global per-object symmetries. On T-LESS, mean MSSD/MSPD scores of existing single-pose methods fall by 2.2 to 29.9 points, and rankings move by up to 6 places: gdrnppdet-pbrrealmegapose-multihyp goes from 12th to 3rd, and only 4 methods exceed the old score. YCB-V changes much less because it has few symmetric objects. The paper also sets up the first precision/recall benchmark for pose-distribution methods on real images. On T-LESS, LiePose-Diffusion reaches R_MSD 75.4 at P_MSD 29.9, and SpyroPose reaches P_MSD 32.8 at R_MSD 48.1. Distribution methods therefore get high recall but low precision. (2) Representations and losses. SARR (IJCV 2026) is a rotation representation that uses the symmetry degree, evaluated on T-LESS and ITODD with a symmetry-sensitive cosine AR. It still needs the symmetry order as input. (3) Distribution and generative outputs. SE(3)-PoseFlow (flow matching on SE(3), Nov 2025) reports state of the art on REAL275, YCB-V and LM-O and uses its pose samples for active perception and grasping. CoordAR (AAAI 2026 oral) reports robustness to symmetry with autoregressive coordinate tokens for one-reference novel objects. Robotics papers such as ActivePose (2025) use FoundationPose entropy and a VLM to choose views that remove the ambiguity. The BOP 2025 challenge (ICCV 2025 R6D workshop) still scores with symmetry-aware MSSD/MSPD/VSD from per-object symmetry annotations. I found no unified metric for finite plus continuous symmetry adopted at a top venue. Applied to hand-held objects, the problem is barely addressed: HO3D/DexYCB-style pipelines still output one pose.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: BOP-Distrib: Revisiting 6D Pose Estimation Benchmarks for Better Evaluation under Visual Ambiguities
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Automatic image-wise re-annotation of the plausible pose sets on BOP datasets, using visible surface. Re-ranks single-pose methods (T-LESS scores -2.2 to -29.9) and adds precision/recall metrics for pose-distribution estimators (SpyroPose, LiePose-Diffusion).

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Towards Symmetry-sensitive Pose Estimation: A Rotation Representation for Symmetric Object Classes (SARR)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Symmetry-degree-aware rotation representation that gives unique, continuous canonical poses. Beats rotation matrices, Euler angles and quaternions on T-LESS and ITODD under a symmetry-sensitive cosine AR. Needs the symmetry order to be known.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: SE(3)-PoseFlow: Estimating 6D Pose Distributions for Uncertainty-Aware Robotic Manipulation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Flow matching on SE(3) for multimodal pose distributions under symmetry, occlusion and partial view. Reports state of the art on REAL275, YCB-V and LM-O and uses the samples for active perception and uncertainty-aware grasping.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: CoordAR: One-Reference 6D Pose Estimation of Novel Objects via Autoregressive Coordinate Map Generation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Tokenizes coordinate maps and decodes them autoregressively, giving probabilistic predictions over discretized 3D space. Targets the failure of coordinate regression under symmetry and occlusion for novel objects with one reference view.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: ActivePose: Active 6D Object Pose Estimation and Tracking for Robotic Manipulation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Uses FoundationPose entropy over rendered CAD views plus VLM ambiguity scores to choose next-best views. A diffusion policy keeps the object in a low-ambiguity view during tracking, so symmetry ambiguity is resolved actively.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: OMNI-PoseX: A Fast Vision Model for 6D Object Pose Estimation in Embodied Tasks
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Open-vocabulary perception combined with an SO(3)-aware reflected flow-matching rotation predictor for unseen objects, used for grasping. How explicitly it handles symmetry is unclear from the abstract.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Symmetry-Aware 9D Pose Estimation with Sim(3)-Consistent Feature and Spherical Inception Convolution (SSH-Pose)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Category-level 9D pose with a semantic-guided symmetry-aware module that infers symmetry from large vision models instead of labels, applied to robotic picking.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Resolving Symmetry Ambiguity in Correspondence-Based Methods for Instance-Level Object Pose Estimation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Symmetry-aware correspondence formulation for instance-level pose. Still relies on known symmetries.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: FreeZeV2 (training-free zero-shot 6D pose with foundation models, symmetry handling)
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Reported to handle geometric symmetry and instance ambiguity for zero-shot pose with visual features. Only seen through search snippets; the V2 paper itself was not opened.

evidence.crowdedness: MEDIUM: about 6-9 relevant papers in 2025-2026, from groups such as Lepetit/CEA (BOP-Distrib), TU Darmstadt/Peters-Chalvatzaki (SE(3)-PoseFlow), TU Wien (SARR) and SJTU (CoordAR), spread across evaluation, representation and generative-distribution angles, with no dominant group or consensus benchmark yet.
evidence.trend: rising: generative and flow-matching pose models and the robotics uptake of uncertainty-aware grasping and active perception are pulling distribution outputs into the mainstream. The BOP-Distrib reranking shows the community that current symmetry-aware metrics mis-score methods. However, the BOP main leaderboard still uses per-object symmetry annotations.

skeptics.reasons: Not refuted, but narrowed. Work from 2025-2026 covers parts of P36 without closing it. (1) Metrics. BOP-Distrib (WACV 2026) re-annotates real images with per-image pose-distribution ground truth based on surface visibility. It adds precision/recall metrics (MPD/MSD) for distribution outputs and shows that rankings of single-pose methods change. This answers the complaint that no metric handles visual ambiguity image by image. Its scope is narrow, though: the distribution ground truth covers T-LESS only, according to the Corr2Distrib description. The BOP Challenge 2024 report (2025) still scores every task, including the new model-free and BOP-H3 hand-object tasks (HOT3D, HOPEv2, HANDAL), with MSSD/MSPD over 'pre-identified global object symmetries'. It does not explain how symmetries are found for model-free onboarding. So the symmetry-label dependency in the main benchmark remains. (2) Multimodal outputs. Corr2Distrib (arXiv 2025), SE(3)-PoseFlow (arXiv 2025, flow matching on SE(3), state of the art on REAL275/YCB-V/LM-O), the depth-only pose-distribution work of Hagelskjaer et al. (ICCR 2025), and the earlier DiffusionNOCS all output pose distributions instead of single poses. This undercuts the 'single deterministic pose' part of the statement for seen or category-level objects. The abstracts I read do not show that any of them generalizes to unseen instances without symmetry or category training, and none of them is a released, standard unseen-object system. (3) Novel objects. The leading unseen-object pipelines (FoundationPose lineage, Any6D at CVPR 2025, FreeZeV2.1, the BOP 2024 winner) still return one pose. Symmetry-aware zero-shot work still injects symmetry priors at training time: WAPR builds the SA6D dataset with rotational symmetry priors; SARR (IJCV 2026) needs symmetry knowledge at training; SAFAG (2026) still needs the symmetry type. I found no released model that infers symmetry automatically for an arbitrary novel object and outputs a calibrated multimodal pose, and no metric that is saturated. The problem is therefore partly addressed (distribution metrics and distribution estimators exist) but not reduced to engineering for unseen objects or hand-held tracking. For the author's field it is adjacent. Hand-object tracking of cups, bottles and bowls inherits the ambiguity, but temporal context and hand contact are extra cues that could collapse it, and the current distribution benchmarks ignore both.

skeptics.reframe: Distribution metrics now exist for seen objects (BOP-Distrib, T-LESS only) and so do distribution estimators (Corr2Distrib, SE(3)-PoseFlow). What remains open is symmetry-label-free ambiguity handling for novel objects that are tracked over time and in hand. Unseen-object pose and tracking systems still output one pose and depend on pre-identified symmetries for training and BOP scoring, including on the BOP-H3 hand-object datasets. No benchmark or method yet uses temporal context or hand contact to resolve or score per-frame symmetry ambiguity of hand-held objects.

skeptics.reasons:
Source diversity is adequate, so the point is not an artifact of one dataset. The 12 papers come from separate groups and settings: BOP organisers (1313), NVIDIA HOPE (1315), PKU Omni6DPose (347), Omni6D (350), ZJU OnePose++ (1325), the GraspNet unseen benchmark (1327), industrial benchmarks XYZ-IBD (402) and IndustryShapes (837), DynOPETs (825), and two surveys (1020, 1088). Two caveats weaken this. First, 1020 and 1328 are the same author line (Thalhammer et al.); 1328 is the withdrawn v1 of essentially the same monocular-challenges survey, so they count as one source. Second, several items are setup-specific: MegaPose training objects lacking symmetry labels in BOP 2023 (1313), OnePose++ numbers on one object, glue (1325), and GenPose energy aggregation (347).

The stated form overclaims on two of its three sub-claims, because another community treated these as managed years ago.
(a) The claim that symmetries must be known at training time is false for an established line of label-free methods. Manhardt et al. (ICCV 2019) output multiple hypotheses. Implicit-PDF (ICML 2021) learns symmetric rotation distributions from single pose labels. SurfEmb (CVPR 2022) is explicitly unsupervised with respect to symmetry. Score-based diffusion on SE(3) (Hsiao et al., CVPR 2024) targets symmetry ambiguity. GenPose failing on discrete symmetries is one method's weakness, not the field's.
(b) The claim that metrics are inconsistent is mostly a convention artifact. ADD and ADD-S belong to the older LINEMOD tradition. Since 2016-2020 the BOP community has used VSD, MSSD and MSPD, with continuous symmetries discretised. Papers that still report ADD(S) are choosing a legacy protocol, not facing an unsolved problem.

What survives is narrower. Symmetry annotations are unavailable for novel or open-vocabulary objects, which come from large CAD or scan collections and in hand-object settings are often reconstructed on the fly. Benchmarks still score a single pose, so multimodal outputs get no credit. No metric handles finite and infinite ambiguity jointly without per-object symmetry labels (1327). In the author's HOI field the issue is only adjacent. HOI papers mostly sidestep it: AlignSDF predicts only translation because of symmetry, and DexYCB/HO3D-style evaluation uses ADD-S-like object errors. That is a real but second-order gap, not a field-level pain point.

skeptics.reframe: For novel objects tracked during hand manipulation, often reconstructed on the fly, symmetry is unknown and the pose posterior is multimodal. Yet trackers output, and benchmarks score, a single pose against per-object symmetry annotations. The open problem is ambiguity-aware tracking and evaluation that needs no symmetry labels, possibly using grasp and contact to disambiguate. Symmetry handling for 6D pose in general is not the open problem: label-free distribution methods and BOP's symmetry-aware metrics already cover it.

skeptics.reasons:
Not refuted. Parts of P36 are just engineering: providing symmetry labels for MegaPose training objects is annotation work, and building yet another symmetry-aware metric beside ADD-S and BOP MSSD/MSPD would struggle to pass review on its own. The core is different. Symmetry is unknown for novel objects, and a single-output regressor cannot represent the set of equivalent poses. That is an open modelling question, not a matter of resources: the fix is not known and waiting to be funded. Recent top-venue work shows that reviewers treat it as significant but unsolved.
- SpyroPose (ICCVW 2023) estimates SE(3) pose distributions, and the record says these "first quantitative results on SE(3) distribution estimation" handle symmetry ambiguity.
- SARR (IJCV 2026) adds a symmetry-sensitive rotation representation but still derives it from known degrees of symmetry.
- Corr2Distrib (arXiv 2025) predicts 6D pose distributions but learns a symmetry-aware representation.
- The P36 evidence shows that GenPose-style energy aggregation fails on the discontinuous multimodal distributions that discrete symmetries create.
- Annotation-free symmetry handling (arXiv 2605.17033, parts pose) is only just appearing.
So label-free, calibrated multimodal pose for unseen objects is live and not saturated.

For this author's field the angle is sharper and less crowded. In hand-object manipulation, visual symmetry interacts with hand occlusion, partial observation and grasp. Contact, grasp configuration and temporal motion can sometimes resolve an ambiguity that appearance alone cannot. The paper "ComPose: When to Trust Hands for Object Pose Tracking" (arXiv 2605.23523) targets exactly this robustness for symmetric objects, which shows the question is current. A task can also make a visually symmetric object functionally asymmetric, for example a mug handle hidden by the hand, or a lid's thread direction. That matters for robot demonstration transfer, so the wrong mode is not harmless.

Research questions a reviewer would find significant:
- (a) Can a tracker infer an object's symmetry group, discrete or continuous, without labels from its own observations, and keep a calibrated posterior over equivalent poses through hand occlusion?
- (b) When do hand pose and contact disambiguate symmetric object pose, and how should a tracker propagate the ambiguity that remains instead of collapsing it?
- (c) Can one evaluation protocol score finite and infinite ambiguity together, including ambiguity caused by occlusion rather than shape, so that set-valued or distributional predictions are rewarded properly?

Caveats that lower the score:
- P36 is tagged adjacent: it sits in generic object pose, where much of the work is incremental symmetry-aware losses and representations.
- The metric sub-problem alone is a weak contribution.
- A thesis author would need to frame the work around hand-object or bimanual ambiguity to avoid competing directly with the BOP community.

skeptics.reframe: In hand-object and bimanual manipulation, an unseen object's pose is ambiguous for three reasons: its shape symmetry, which is unknown, the hand hiding part of it, and a task that can make a visually symmetric object functionally asymmetric. Current trackers need symmetry labels and output one pose. They are scored with metrics that cannot reward a set of equally valid answers. The open question is whether a tracker can (i) discover an object's equivalence set without labels from its own observations, (ii) use hand pose, contact and motion over time to resolve that ambiguity, and keep a calibrated multimodal posterior when it cannot, and (iii) be evaluated with one protocol that covers finite, infinite and occlusion-induced ambiguity.

research_questions.question: Can a tracker of a hand-held object whose mesh is given or reconstructed, but whose symmetry labels are not, keep a calibrated multimodal posterior over the object's pose during manipulation? The idea is that it (a) finds the object's ambiguity set at test time from rendered self-similarity of the mesh, with no labels, and (b) uses the rigid hand-object coupling during a stable grasp, together with time, to carry the identity of a symmetry-breaking feature through hand occlusion (for example a mug handle or a can label that the hand covers). The test is whether this cuts mode flips and errors on the parts that matter for the task, compared with single-pose foundation trackers, without hurting objects that are not symmetric.
research_questions.why_top_venue: The three skeptics' reframes meet at this gap. Unseen-object trackers (the FoundationPose lineage, Any6D) and hand-object pipelines still output one pose and are scored against global per-object symmetries. SHOW3D (Meta, arXiv 2603.28760, Mar 2026; quote verified) reports that its in-the-wild hand-object annotation pipeline 'correctly tracks the 3D position but fails to resolve the azimuthal rotation' of a near-symmetric object with a thin handle. ComPose (arXiv 2605.23523, May 2026; abstract verified) uses hand joints as a cue for occluded object tracking but outputs one trajectory, and its abstract does not mention symmetry or distributions. PoseRBPF (RSS 2019 / T-RO 2021; verified) tracks a full rotation distribution for symmetric objects, but only for known objects with per-object trained codebooks and without hand cues. BOP-Distrib (WACV 2026; abstract verified) defines ambiguity per image from visible surface but does not cover hand-object data. Putting together test-time ambiguity discovery, hand-coupled propagation and calibrated posteriors on standard hand-object benchmarks would be a new and clearly stated contribution for CVPR, ICCV or ECCV, if the effect is large on the affected objects.
research_questions.method_sketch: 1) Test-time ambiguity set. Render the object mesh (CAD or reconstructed) from a dense SO(3) grid. Compare renders with depth plus frozen DINOv2 features and keep the rotations g for which the object is indistinguishable within a tolerance tied to sensor noise. This gives a discrete or continuous self-similarity set G with no labels, as a cheap test-time stand-in for BOP's offline symmetry annotation. 2) Filter. Use a Rao-Blackwellized particle filter in the style of PoseRBPF: translation comes from depth and the refiner, and rotation particles are seeded on the orbit G times the refined pose. The likelihood is the frozen FoundationPose refiner plus scorer, with its score temperature-calibrated on held-out frames so that it acts as a likelihood. 3) Hand-coupled motion model. Hand pose comes from WiLoR or HaMeR, and the contact state is detected from hand-surface proximity in depth. During a detected stable grasp, each particle stores the object-in-hand transform and is propagated with the wrist motion, so the mode chosen while the handle was visible survives occlusion. A switching model (grasp / slip / release) with a small transition probability guards against in-hand slip and regrasp. 4) Output. Report weighted modes plus a MAP pose. When the visible surface breaks the symmetry, the posterior collapses; while it does not, the remaining multimodality is kept rather than collapsed.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Pilot (4-6 weeks, go/no-go). On public DexYCB and HO3D v3 sequences with symmetric or near-symmetric YCB objects (for example the mug, bowl, cans, pitcher base, bleach cleanser and large marker; the exact list must be checked against each dataset's object set), run FoundationPose tracking. Measure (a) the fraction of frames where the hand-occluded visible surface admits more than one pose mode, and (b) FoundationPose's rate of mode flips against ground truth. Continue only if both are non-trivial; as a working threshold, at least about 5 percent of frames on the affected objects show a real handle or label flip. Full study: our filter against FoundationPose tracking, per-frame FoundationPose re-initialization, the filter without hand coupling (a PoseRBPF-style ablation), and the filter without test-time G (seeded from the BOP global symmetry). Metrics: BOP MSSD/MSPD AR (the standard metric), distribution precision/recall against hand-aware per-frame ambiguity ground truth (from research question 2), mode-flip rate per minute, error on task-relevant parts (handle or spout direction), negative control on asymmetric objects, and runtime on one GPU. Add a small real set on the author's desk rig: a near-symmetric mug whose ArUco base plate gives a metric pose that breaks the symmetry, with the marker masked out of the method's input.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: Public data: DexYCB (multi-view, YCB objects, MANO hands), HO3D v3 (public ground-truth splits only), HOT3D in BOP-H3 format (public ground-truth splits), YCB meshes, BOP toolkit. Frozen models: FoundationPose (NVIDIA research licence, to be checked), WiLoR or HaMeR, DINOv2. Hardware: one workstation GPU with 24 GB (RTX 3090/4090 class); the filter runs offline at roughly 50-100 rotation hypotheses per frame and does not need to be real time for the paper. One consumer RGB-D camera for the small real validation set. No motion capture and no robot needed.
research_questions.risks: (1) Effect size. Truly symmetric objects produce geometrically harmless ambiguity, so the gain is confined to near-symmetric objects during occlusion windows. Aggregate AR may barely move, and reviewers may call per-subset metrics cherry-picked. Pre-register the subset definition from the per-frame ambiguity ground truth. (2) Scoop risk. ComPose (KAIST/Yonsei line), Meta's HOT3D/SHOW3D/BOP-H3 team and the CEA BOP-Distrib group are each one step away. (3) Novelty may be read as 'PoseRBPF plus FoundationPose plus a hand prior'. The contribution must rest on label-free test-time G and calibrated hand-coupled propagation, with ablations proving each. (4) FoundationPose scores are not calibrated likelihoods, and calibration may not transfer across objects. (5) Hand-estimator failure under heavy occlusion, in-hand rotation and slip break the rigid-coupling assumption. (6) The tolerance thresholds that define 'indistinguishable' are magic numbers that set the result and must be tied to sensor noise and reported as a sweep. (7) Ground-truth poses of symmetric objects in some datasets may themselves be ambiguous or noisy.

research_questions.question: For hand-held objects, can a single evaluation protocol define pose equivalence per frame as indistinguishable visible surface given the actual hand occlusion? Such a protocol would cover finite symmetry, continuous symmetry and ambiguity caused by hand occlusion of symmetry-breaking parts in one definition, and could score both single-pose and distribution trackers. The question is whether it changes the conclusions drawn from the current global-symmetry MSSD/MSPD scoring on hand-object benchmarks.
research_questions.why_top_venue: BOP-Distrib showed that image-wise ambiguity ground truth reorders single-pose methods on T-LESS by up to 6 places, with score drops of 2.2 to 29.9 points (figures from the evidence record; the abstract is verified, the per-dataset numbers were not re-opened). The BOP Challenge 2024 report still scores the hand-object tasks (HOT3D, HOPEv2, HANDAL) against pre-identified global symmetries (skeptic evidence, not re-opened). No hand-object benchmark accounts for occlusion by the hand, which is the dominant occluder by construction. On its own the metric is a weak contribution (skeptic 3). As the evaluation backbone of research question 1, or as a datasets-and-benchmarks paper with re-ranking results and released annotations, it is publishable.
research_questions.method_sketch: For each evaluated frame, render the ground-truth object and the ground-truth MANO hand meshes, which gives the visible object surface after hand occlusion. Search SO(3) around the ground-truth pose, seeded by the self-similarity set G from research question 1, for poses whose visible surface (depth plus a texture or feature residual) matches within a noise-derived tolerance. This yields a per-frame equivalence set S_t. Single-pose error is the minimum MSSD/MSPD over S_t. It reduces to standard MSSD for global symmetries, and to the strict error when the hand leaves the symmetry-breaking part visible. Distribution outputs get precision/recall against S_t in the BOP-Distrib style. Add a temporal term: mode consistency, which penalizes flips between modes of S_t that a physical object cannot make while grasped rigidly.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: Re-annotate the symmetric and near-symmetric object frames of the public-ground-truth DexYCB and HOT3D splits, subsampling frames if rendering cost requires it. Re-score 4-6 public trackers and estimators (for example FoundationPose, MegaPose, Any6D, the BundleSDF-style model-free tracking, and ComPose if code is released) under global-symmetry MSSD and under the hand-aware protocol. Report ranking changes, the per-object share of ambiguous frames, and agreement of the automatic S_t with a small manually checked sample (about 200 frames) as an annotation-validity check.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: DexYCB and HOT3D public-ground-truth splits with MANO hand ground truth, YCB/HOT3D meshes, BOP toolkit, and a GPU rasterizer (nvdiffrast or pyrender). One 24 GB GPU; rendering at the order of thousands of SO(3) samples per frame needs frame subsampling and days, not weeks. No new capture is needed.
research_questions.risks: (1) Weak as a standalone contribution, and reviewers may see it as BOP-Distrib applied to new data unless hand occlusion and the temporal term change the conclusions. (2) Test-set ground truth for some benchmarks (HO3D v3 evaluation, BOP-H3 test) is withheld, which limits the protocol to public splits. (3) The tolerance choice defines S_t, so it must be justified and swept. (4) Adoption depends on the BOP organisers; a small lab cannot make it the standard. (5) Whether the BOP-Distrib code and annotations are released was not verified.
target_venues: or folded into the CVPR/ECCV paper of research question 1

research_questions.question: When a demonstrated object is visually near-symmetric but functionally asymmetric (a mug handle, a pitcher spout, a bottle cap or nozzle), does passing a calibrated pose posterior instead of a single pose from human-demonstration tracking to a robot planner reduce failed transfers? Can the remaining ambiguity drive an action that resolves it, such as a viewpoint change or a disambiguating regrasp?
research_questions.why_top_venue: Robotics venues are taking up pose distributions for grasping and active perception (SE(3)-PoseFlow, ActivePose; both arXiv 2025 and verified by the evidence agent). Joyce et al. (arXiv 2512.01856, Dec 2025; abstract verified) evaluate pose estimators by simulated grasping. No work found ties hand-object demonstration tracking, functional asymmetry and the cost of the wrong mode in downstream transfer. This is a natural robotics extension of research question 1, but secondary.
research_questions.method_sketch: Take the posterior from research question 1 on DexYCB and HO3D demonstrations. Retarget each demonstration in simulation (ManiSkill, Isaac or PyBullet with YCB models) to a gripper or dexterous hand, where the task needs the functional part (grasp the handle, pour from the spout). Compare three conditions: (a) the single MAP pose; (b) a posterior-aware planner that picks the grasp with the highest expected success over modes, or asks for a view change when the expected success under the mode distribution falls below a threshold; (c) the ground-truth pose as an upper bound.
research_questions.minimum_experiment: A simulated task-success study on about 5 near-symmetric YCB objects over a few hundred retargeted demonstrations. Report task success, the wrong-mode failure rate and the number of extra views requested. A real-robot run is optional and only with a borrowed arm.
research_questions.data_and_hardware: DexYCB and HO3D demonstrations, YCB meshes, an open-source simulator, the same single GPU. A real robot is needed only for a CoRL-grade claim, and the lab does not have one.
research_questions.risks: (1) CoRL and RSS reviewers usually expect real-robot results; without an arm this is limited to ICRA/RA-L. (2) Sim retargeting of human grasps is itself brittle and may swamp the pose-mode effect. (3) Functional asymmetry has to be annotated per object (which part matters), which is light but manual. (4) The gain exists only if research question 1 already shows frequent mode errors.

fit.thesis_assets_help: Small. Four assets help at the margin. (1) The ArUco-marked object with metric pose. A near-symmetric mug on a marked base plate gives a symmetry-breaking ground truth while the hand covers the handle, if the marker is masked out of the method's input. That makes a small real validation set for research question 1, not a benchmark. (2) The measured/held/constrained honesty labels. These per-frame evidence-source labels anticipate the posterior's states: collapsed by observation, propagated through occlusion, inferred from hand coupling. This is a useful conceptual bridge and a framing aid. (3) The causal 30 fps chain and the Unity twin. They help a real-time online demo and a digital-twin visualization of mode sets, but are not needed for the paper's claims. (4) Object-conditioned recovery of the occluded arm. It runs the coupling in the opposite direction (object to arm), so the code transfers only loosely to hand-to-object propagation. The 28 recordings of one subject cannot serve as evaluation data at a top venue. The edge is a quicker start on one real-data figure and a ready framing, not a competitive advantage.
fit.what_a_small_lab_cannot_do_here:
Seven things are out of reach. (1) It cannot train a foundation-scale unseen-object pose network or SE(3) flow-matching or diffusion distribution model on million-image synthetic sets (MegaPose, FoundationPose or SE(3)-PoseFlow scale); it has to build on frozen models at test time. (2) It cannot compete on the general BOP leaderboard or on symmetry-aware representations for seen objects (SARR, Corr2Distrib), where well-resourced groups dominate. (3) It cannot capture a new large hand-object dataset with symmetry-breaking ground truth at HOT3D or SHOW3D scale (multi-view rigs, motion capture, many subjects). Real data is limited to a small single-camera validation set. (4) It cannot make a new metric the community standard without BOP organiser adoption. (5) It cannot run CoRL- or RSS-grade real-robot evaluation without a borrowed arm. (6) It cannot outpace Meta (HOT3D/SHOW3D/BOP-H3), the ComPose group or the CEA BOP-Distrib group if they target hand-occlusion ambiguity directly, so the pilot must be fast and the scope narrow. (7) It cannot meet real-time multi-hypothesis rendering at 30 fps with FoundationPose-class scoring on one GPU, so the main claims should be offline.

Verification notes. Opened this session: the abstracts of ComPose 2605.23523 (no mention of symmetry or distributions), BOP-Distrib 2408.17297 (it does not state which datasets were re-annotated or whether code is released), Temporally Consistent 6D Pose 2605.02708 (factor graph; no symmetry handling stated), 2606.16593 (it assumes rotational symmetry, does not infer it) and 2512.01856 (simulated grasp evaluation; no symmetry stated), plus the symmetry passage in SHOW3D 2603.28760. PoseRBPF's symmetric-object distribution tracking was confirmed through search results only. Taken from the evidence and skeptic records without re-opening: the T-LESS-only scope of the BOP-Distrib ground truth, the BOP 2024 hand-object tasks using global symmetries, and the DexYCB/HO3D object lists. The DexYCB/HO3D object lists are from memory and must be checked.

painpoint.name: Dynamic neural reconstruction fails under articulated motion and occlusion

evidence.latest_state: Dynamic NVS of hands, hand-held objects and moving people improved in 2025-2026 only where strong priors or extra sensing are added. The problem stays open for general, prior-free, ego-moving, long and fast sequences. The Ego-1K paper (CVPR 2026) reports held-out PSNR of 16.46 for K-Planes, 21.22 for per-frame 3DGS and 24.76 for Spacetime Gaussians. A stereo-guided 3DGS variant reaches 29.12, but it needs rectified stereo, and the gap grows when hands are close to the camera. Interaction-Aware 4DGS (arXiv 2511.14540) is prior-free. It reaches PSNR 30.32 on HOI4D translation scenes but only 24.16 on translation-plus-rotation scenes, where the best baseline, Deform3DGS, scores 23.57. On HO3D it scores 25.19 against 20.37 for SC-GS, and the authors say it fails on very fast motion and complex trajectories. Template-anchored methods get robustness from MANO or diffusion priors: DyTact (2D Gaussian surfels on MANO with contact-guided sampling, 3DV 2026 oral), BIGS (bimanual 3DGS with SDS priors for hidden object surfaces, CVPR 2025) and Hand-4DGS (feed-forward, about 60 FPS, evaluated on H2O and ARCTIC, arXiv 2606.19156). Their abstracts still list fast head motion, rapid hand dynamics and severe occlusion as unsolved. In egocentric settings, DP-DeGauss (arXiv 2604.07986) reports +1.70 dB average PSNR from splitting background, hand and object. A CVPR 2026 EgoVis workshop study on EgoExo4D finds egocentric reconstruction quality consistently below exocentric quality. For the body and avatar side, TaoGS (SIGGRAPH Asia 2025) handles topology changes such as changing clothes and long-term tracking in volumetric video. I did not find, and the abstract does not give, a re-benchmark on ActorsHQ-length sequences. I also found no 2025-2026 method reporting results that close the DiVa-360 gap between interaction and object-only sequences, or the NVS-HO gap.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Ego-1K - A Large-Scale Multiview Video Dataset for Egocentric Vision
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Releases about 1,000 egocentric multiview videos (12 rig cameras plus a Quest 3) of hand motion and hand-object interaction. Benchmarks 3D and 4D NVS: K-Planes 16.46, per-frame 3DGS 21.22, Spacetime Gaussians 24.76 and stereo-guided 3DGS 29.12 PSNR. Shows that dynamic methods fail under ego-motion combined with near-range hands.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Interaction-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Reconstructs hand-object interaction with 4DGS and no object prior, using interaction-aware Gaussians, a piecewise-linear motion assumption and progressive optimization. Reaches HOI4D PSNR 30.32 (translation) and 24.16 (translation plus rotation), and HO3D 25.19 against 20.37 for SC-GS. The authors say it fails on very rapid motion.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: DyTact: Capturing Dynamic Contacts in Hand-Object Manipulation
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Uses dynamic articulated 2D Gaussian surfels bound to MANO, with contact-guided adaptive sampling against occlusion and a deformation refinement module. Claims state-of-the-art contact estimation and NVS for hand-object manipulation.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: BIGS: Bimanual Category-agnostic Interaction Reconstruction from Monocular Videos via 3D Gaussian Splatting
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Reconstructs two hands and an unknown object from monocular video using 3DGS, MANO constraints and diffusion SDS priors to fill object surfaces hidden by severe bimanual occlusion. Reports hand MPJPE, object Chamfer distance and F-score, and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Hand-4DGS: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for 4D Hand Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Feed-forward, mesh-anchored Gaussians with temporal convolutions for dynamic egocentric hands at about 60 FPS, without per-video optimization, evaluated on H2O and ARCTIC. The abstract lists fast head motion, rapid hand dynamics and severe occlusion as challenges.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: DP-DeGauss: Dynamic Probabilistic Gaussian Decomposition for Egocentric 4D Scene Reconstruction
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Splits egocentric 4D scenes into background, hand and object Gaussians under ego-motion and occlusion. Reports +1.70 dB average PSNR over baselines.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: Bringing a Personal Point of View: Evaluating Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Scene Reconstruction
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Evaluates monocular dynamic 3DGS on paired ego and exo EgoExo4D recordings. Egocentric quality is consistently lower, and the PSNR gap comes mostly from static content under head motion.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: TaoGS: Topology-Aware Optimization of Gaussian Primitives for Human-Centric Volumetric Videos
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Uses sparse motion Gaussians driven by a spatio-temporal tracker, with locally activated appearance Gaussians, for long-term tracking and topology changes (for example, changing clothes) in human volumetric video. Compresses up to 40x.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: CHOIR: Contact-aware 4D Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Reconstructs 4D hand-object interaction from monocular video in three stages: visual-prior initialization, generative spatial rectification and contact-aware optimization. Targets clutter, occlusion and unseen geometry, with a focus on geometry and pose rather than NVS.

attacking_papers_2025_2026.title: CARI4D: Category Agnostic 4D Reconstruction of Human-Object Interaction
attacking_papers_2025_2026.what_it_does: Reconstructs 4D human-object interaction at metric scale from monocular RGB, using foundation-model pose hypotheses, render-and-compare refinement and contact reasoning. Known only from the search snippet; I did not open the paper.

evidence.crowdedness: MEDIUM: I found about 10 directly relevant 2025-2026 papers from several strong groups (Meta/Ego-1K, Brown/Sridhar, KAIST/Baek, ETH/Pollefeys with Yonsei, MPI/Theobalt with ShanghaiTech, SJTU, Oxford/UCL/CUHK). Most of them avoid the core failure by adding a MANO template, diffusion priors or stereo, rather than solving prior-free dynamic NVS under ego-motion and occlusion.
evidence.trend: Rising: new multiview egocentric benchmarks (Ego-1K at CVPR 2026, MultiEgo) and egocentric 4DGS work in 2026, driven by smart glasses and robot-data capture, are increasing attention. The trend is toward feed-forward, template-anchored 4D Gaussian methods and away from per-scene deformation fields.

skeptics.reasons:
No 2025-2026 work I found solves P37 or turns it into engineering, but a lot of it reduces the hand-object half, and the pain point as written is too broad.

What has improved:
- Prior-driven monocular methods now handle occlusion better. BIGS (CVPR 2025) uses MANO and diffusion score distillation (SDS) to fill in unseen object parts with two hands. Interaction-Aware 4DGS (arXiv 2511.14540) handles tight two-hand grasps without object priors, from multi-view or monocular RGB-D input. HOIGS (arXiv 2604.04016) separates human and object deformation.
- Feed-forward 4D Gaussian models have arrived. 4DGT (arXiv 2506.08015) reconstructs long real-world monocular videos in seconds. Hand-4DGS (arXiv 2606.19156) reconstructs egocentric 4D hands at about 60 FPS on H2O and ARCTIC.
- Grasp in Gaussians (arXiv 2604.12929, Theobalt group) gets temporally coherent long hand-object sequences 4.4x to 38.9x faster than prior work.

Why this does not refute it:
1. None of these papers shows a saturated metric on DiVa-360, Ego-1K, NVS-HO or ActorsHQ. The pain-point record gives a median foreground PSNR of about 16 on NVS-HO and 29 at best on Ego-1K, with stereo guidance.
2. The fixes push the problem into strong priors: MANO, SDS hallucination, SAM3D-style object initialisation. Grasp in Gaussians drops heavy neural representations in favour of tracking, which suggests the field is going around photoreal dynamic hand-object reconstruction rather than solving it.
3. Hand-4DGS covers hands only, with no hand-held object. Its own abstract lists fast head motion, rapid hand dynamics and severe occlusion as open challenges.
4. 4DGT needs posed video and is not built for near-range manipulation.
5. A 2026 HOI foundation-model survey (arXiv 2607.28394) still calls HOI severely uncertain visually.

The avatar half (hair, sway in the OLAT light stage, long-sequence memory) is adjacent to the author's field. It is partly an engineering and capture issue, for example optical-flow motion compensation, and it weakens the pain point as a single coherent problem. The search budget was small, so a 2026 benchmark result could have been missed.

skeptics.reframe: Narrow the pain point to hand-object scenes and drop the avatar and hair cases. Photoreal, temporally consistent 4D reconstruction of an unknown hand-held object together with the manipulating hands, from monocular or egocentric RGB(-D) with camera motion, is still open: object pose and occluded appearance are coupled, so pose errors and hand occlusion together cap foreground quality (about 16 dB foreground PSNR on NVS-HO). Current methods either hallucinate the occluded parts with priors (MANO, diffusion SDS) or give up on appearance and only track geometry. Feed-forward 4D models (4DGT, Hand-4DGS) do not yet cover hand-held objects.

skeptics.reasons:
Partly refuted as stated. In its favour, the 11 papers are not from one group or one setup. They include a Brown table-scale dome (DiVa-360, GigaHands), a 12-camera egocentric rig (Ego-1K), a static camera with a hand-rotated object (NVS-HO), and studio, head and light-stage avatar captures (HumanRF/ActorsHQ, NeRSemble, RenderMe-360, HumanOLAT). The general claim that dynamic NVS degrades under complex motion is also supported independently: DyCheck (Gao et al., NeurIPS 2022, verified) reported a 4-5 dB masked-PSNR drop for complex motion on realistic monocular video. That part is not an artifact of one dataset.

Three things narrow it.

(1) Every benchmark number comes from generic, template-free dynamic baselines: per-frame I-NGP, MixVoxels, K-Planes, Spacetime Gaussians, Splatfacto and HumanRF. Running those baselines is a convention of dataset papers. The hand-object community has handled articulated hand motion for some time by driving Gaussians or implicit fields with a MANO hand model. Examples are HOLD (CVPR 2024 Highlight, category-agnostic monocular hand+object), MANUS (CVPR 2024, articulated 3D Gaussians from 50+ cameras), BIGS (CVPR 2025, bimanual with an unknown object, using a diffusion prior on unseen object parts; object F-score 83.93 vs HOLD 63.92 on ARCTIC) and GHOST (arXiv 2603.18912, 2026, an order of magnitude faster). So "fails under articulated motion" mostly describes baselines the field has already moved past. It is not a measured failure of hand-object-specific methods.

(2) The statement joins two problems. Half of it comes from the avatar and clinical community: fast hair motion, subjects swaying during an 11 s OLAT capture, and long full-body sequences with topology changes. That half concerns capture logistics and head or body deformation, not manipulation, which matches its 'adjacent' relevance label.

(3) Some numbers are small or setup-specific. HumanRF loses 1.25 dB going from 20 to 1000 frames. The K-Planes gap on DiVa-360 is only 0.44 dB. The NVS-HO failure is mostly a pose-estimation failure (COLMAP on a handheld object), not a failure of the representation.

What survives is narrower. Ego-1K and NVS-HO point to photoreal, temporally consistent reconstruction of an unknown hand-held object when the camera moves or is egocentric and the hand hides much of the object. The template-driven methods above still assume a mostly static monocular or dense multi-view camera and optimise each sequence slowly. That narrower point is a real research problem.

skeptics.reframe: Hand-object methods that use a hand model (HOLD, MANUS, BIGS, GHOST) cope with hand articulation, but they still assume a mostly static or dense multi-view camera and optimise each sequence slowly. Nothing yet produces a photoreal, temporally consistent 4D reconstruction of an unknown hand-held object when the camera moves (egocentric or handheld) and the hand hides much of the object. In that case the object pose and the hidden surface have to be recovered together without a template; Ego-1K and NVS-HO show general dynamic NVS and pose-from-COLMAP pipelines failing here.

skeptics.reasons: Refutation attempt fails for the hand-object core of P37, but succeeds for parts of its scope. The bundled statement mixes three things. (1) The avatar and light-stage items (subject sway during 11 s OLAT capture, memory budgets for 1000-frame HumanRF sequences, per-frame mask flicker) are largely engineering or capture-protocol issues with known remedies (flow compensation, chunked or streaming representations, better matting) and on their own yield no top-venue question; they are also off-field for this author. (2) The hand-object part is a live research problem, not a data or money problem: the evidence shows the failure is structural. NVS-HO reports pose refinement gives only marginal gains and foreground PSNR around 16; DiVa-360 shows a consistent 0.4-2.7 dB drop on interaction vs object-only sequences in a 53-camera dome, so more cameras do not solve it; Ego-1K shows dynamic models built for fixed-pose multiview fail under ego-motion plus near-range hands. The cause stated in why_it_persists (canonical-plus-smooth-deformation or accurate-pose assumptions violated by articulation, contact and mutual occlusion) is a modelling assumption, which is the shape of a publishable question. (3) Top venues are actively publishing exactly this: MANUS (CVPR 2024, articulated 3D Gaussians for grasp capture), HOLD (CVPR 2024, category-agnostic hand-object reconstruction from monocular video), BIGS (CVPR 2025, bimanual category-agnostic interaction via 3DGS), plus 2025-2026 arXiv follow-ups (interaction-aware 4D Gaussians, Grasp in Gaussians, CHOIR contact-aware 4D HOI, physics-aware multi-view 4D HOI Gaussians). This confirms reviewers find the question significant, but also that the space is crowded: a generic 'better dynamic Gaussians for hands' paper will be judged incremental. Remaining significant questions a reviewer would accept: how to jointly recover hand articulation, unknown-object 6DoF pose and appearance when pose error and occlusion are coupled (the object is seen only where the hand is not, and pose is estimated only from what is seen); how to keep a reconstruction temporally consistent over long sequences with regrasps and bimanual handovers where contact changes topology; and whether depth (RGB-D) or physical contact constraints break the pose-appearance circularity from a single static camera, where NVS-HO shows current methods fail. Score held at 6 not higher because the relevance is adjacent (rendering quality/PSNR is not the author's metric), the subfield is crowded with strong groups, and half the evidence base (avatars, OLAT) contributes no question.
